articles.title_orig: World leaders reaffirm support for UN peacekeeping at the General Assembly amid mounting financial pressures
articles.title_zh: World leaders reaffirm support for UN peacekeeping at the General Assembly amid mounting financial pressures
articles.content_orig:
Every year in September, heads of state and government, foreign ministers and other senior officials from around the world gather in New York City for the High-level Week of the UN General Assembly (UNGA).
During the General Debate, representatives of Member States, as well as the European Union, the State of Palestine and the Holy See, present their views on some of the world’s most pressing challenges, including peace and security, human rights, development, the environment and international cooperation.
This year’s 81 st session took place against the backdrop of an unprecedented liquidity crisis, including significant pressure on the UN peacekeeping budget. Last August, in response to the Pact for the Future, UN Secretary-General António Guterres conducted a review on the future of all forms of United Nations peace operations. The report highlighted the importance of UN peacekeeping in maintaining international peace and security, while acknowledging the need for UN peace operations to adapt to increasingly complex environments through more focused mandates, stronger partnerships with host countries and predictable, adequate and sustained financing.
So, what did Member States say about UN peacekeeping this year?
More financing for peacekeeping is needed.
One of the most frequent messages from Member States during the UNGA debate was the need for sustainable and predictable financing for UN peacekeeping, with several warning that budget cuts could reduce missions’ ability to deliver on their mandates.
Faustin Archange Touadera, Head of State of the Central African Republic, emphasized “ peacekeeping operations, including in [his] own country, have been forced to cut back their patrols, shut down bases, and suspend local dialogue initiatives. Each budget cut adopted in New York or in some faraway capital is an opportunity for armed groups on the ground.”
Barbados Prime Minister, Mia Amor Mottley, emphasized these concerns: “ Transformation and development, peacekeeping and humanitarian aid cannot succeed if Member States are unwilling to fund it. ”
The call for adequate financing was also echoed by France, a permanent member of the Security Council. “ Peace operations must be more effective and to this end they must be enabled, endowed with adequate funding and better coordinated ,” said President Emmanuel Macron.
Gabon, Poland, Portugal, Romania, and Zimbabwe also called for stable and adequate funding for peacekeeping operations to support more effective missions and sustainable peace.
Strong support for UN peacekeeping.
Many Member States that spoke about UN peacekeeping also highlighted their own countries’ military and police contributions around the world.
Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, Guatemala, India, Indonesia, Mongolia, Pakistan and the Soloman Islands all emphasized their personnel contributions to UN peacekeeping missions—military, police and civilian.
Feleti Teo, Prime Minister of Tuvalu, made an impactful statement: “ This year also marks the historical and first deployment of Tuvalu police officers to serve in the UN Mission in South Sudan, a deployment that confirms that even the smallest member of the UN can contribute meaningfully to international peace and security. ”
Other leaders reflected more broadly on the value of peacekeeping and the service of those deployed under the UN flag, often at great personal cost.
President of Uruguay, Yamandú Orsi, said: “ Uruguayan men and women can bear witness to the value of this instrument in easing suffering and guaranteeing respect for the human lives of the most defenseless populations. ”
William Samoei Ruto, President of Kenya, acknowledged the important work of all UN peacekeepers highlighting “ More than two million peacekeepers have served under the UN flag, proving that peace can be built, protected and sustained .”
While many Member States noted the service of their personnel serving in peacekeeping, several nations including Brunei Darussalam, Ireland and Lebanon paid tribute to the UN peacekeepers who lost their lives serving under the blue flag.
Nawaf Salam, President of the Council of Ministers of Lebanon, heartfully thanked all those who have served in the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) , whose mandate ends at the end of the year. “ I must pay tribute to the role played by the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon, UNIFIL, and to the courage of its leadership, personnel and staff and their sacrifices in preserving stability, supporting the Lebanese Armed forces and implementing resolution 1701, ” he said.
" To all the countries that have contributed troops to this force, Lebanon extends its profound thanks and appreciation, ” he added.
The importance of women in UN peacekeeping.
The role of women in peacekeeping was also prominent in the debate.
Setting the stage with his opening remarks, Secretary-General António Guterres emphasized that “ peace is more durable when women are at the table. ”
Khurelsukh Ukhnaa, President of Mongolia, underscored his country’s commitment to the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda and increasing women’s participation in peacekeeping.
“ Mongolia has been actively advancing the implementation of United Nations Security Council resolution 1325 , ” he stressed, adding that his country has become one of the few to have reached 15 percent women’s participation and representation among its military personnel serving in UN peacekeeping operations.
Prime Minister of Bangladesh, Tarique Rahman, stated his nations support noting “ The courageous participation of Bangladeshi women in peacekeeping missions, even under adverse circumstances, reflects our strong commitment to advancing the agenda of Women, Peace and Security. ”
In reflections of post-conflict settings, President of Namibia Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah praised the positive impact of the WPS agenda, explaining it “ has contributed positively to the rehabilitation, reconciliation, and reintegration efforts in conflict-affected regions, serving as a core framework for stabilizing post-conflict situations. ”
Luxembourg and Tunisia also highlighted the importance of gender inclusion and its impact on peace.
Building sustainable peace and national capacity
Another key topic of discussion at the general debate was the need for capacity building in peacekeeping to support missions in transition. This included more institution strengthening, peacebuilding and support for long-term national ownership.
The Permanent Representative of South Sudan to the United Nations, Cecilia Adout Majok Adeng, emphasized “ the objective must be a South Sudan capable of sustaining its own peace."
Mohamed Ali Nafti, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Migration and Tunisians abroad, shared that his country “ firmly believes that peace operations cannot be limited to crisis management and conflict containment, but must contribute to creating the conditions conducive to building sustainable peace, through supporting State institutions, strengthening the rule of law, empowering local communities and promoting development. ”
Among the issues highlighted by host countries was the need for sustained international support as UN peacekeeping missions draw down and eventually depart. This included the Central African Republic (CAR) that hosts the United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic (MINUSCA) and Lebanon which hosts UNIFIL.
“ The Central African Republic, like all sovereign nations, aspires to take full charge of its own security, ” said Faustin Archange Touadéra, Head of State. “ And I say this with the same gravity: Any drawdown of MINUSCA ought to be gradual, based upon objective and agreed criteria, and not be based on an arbitrary timeline untethered from realities on the ground. ”

articles.title_orig: The Midterm Senate Fight Spreads to a Surprising New Battleground
articles.title_zh: The Midterm Senate Fight Spreads to a Surprising New Battleground
articles.content_orig:
Democrats are dreaming of a revolution in Kansas in November, trying to believe in polling that shows a tight race in the Senate contest there between the Democrat, Rev. Adam Hamilton, and the Republican incumbent, Sen. Roger Marshall.
It would indeed be a watershed moment if Hamilton takes the seat: No Democrat has won a Senate seat in Kansas since 1932, not quite a century but a very, very long time.
In fact, since Kansas became a state in 1861, only three Democrats have represented it in the Senate. It’s a remarkable statistic since the two parties have evolved so much during that time.
Related: Read a Q and A with a Kansas-based political expert from CNN’s What Matters newsletter about why Kansas has stayed Republican at the Senate level for so long and why Kansans feel targeted by some of Trump’s policies this year.
While American politics seem locked in place; 30 of the 50 states have been represented by a senator from both parties during this century. And while the states that have been represented by both parties most recently track closely with the swing states that decide elections, there are a few exceptions, like Montana and Alabama.
No Republican has been elected to represent the islands since 1970. That Republican, Hiram Fong, was one of Hawaii’s two first senators, elected when Hawaii became a state in 1959. No Democrat has been elected to represent Wyoming or Utah since that same year.
The longest streak east of the Mississippi River is in New Jersey, where no Republican has been elected to the US Senate since Clifford Case was elected in 1972, capping a long career on Capitol Hill. A Republican senator, Jeffrey Chiesa, was briefly appointed to serve in 2013. That was the result of the state having a Republican governor, Chris Christie, at the time.
The Senate is up for grabs. Plot each party’s best path to winning
A Kansas voter would have to be well over 100 years old to have voted for the state’s last Democratic senator, but the current governor is a Democrat.
In New Hampshire, the state is represented by two Democratic senators. The last Republican elected was Kelly Ayotte in 2010. She’s currently the state’s governor. And Republicans hope that another former senator, John Sununu, can break the trend and reclaim a Senate seat this year. When he served as senator, the state had two Republican senators.
Far fewer states are sending a split delegation — both a Republican and a Democratic senator — than ever before in US history. Since the nationwide election of senators began with the 1914 election after the ratification of the 17th amendment, there have generally been at least 10 and frequently more than 20 split delegations, according to a 2021 analysis by Pew .
Currently there are only four: Vermont, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin — none of which has a Senate race this year — and Maine, where Republican Sen. Susan Collins is among the most endangered incumbents. If she loses to Democrat Troy Jackson, Maine will join the wave of states bringing their senators in line with their status as blue or red for presidential purposes. And Collins is one of the few true moderates of either party left in the chamber.
The other senator from Maine, Angus King, is an independent, but like Sen. Bernie Sanders in Vermont, he sides with Democrats in procedural matters, making him a Democrat for purposes of determining which party controls the Senate.
The last time Vermont elected a Republican, Sen. Jim Jeffords in 2000, he ended up switching parties when Republicans angered him. There’s conjecture now that Pennsylvania’s Democratic Sen. John Fetterman might soon do the inverse, but he has insisted that he will remain a Democrat.
There’s Pennsylvania precedent for party-switching. Sen. Arlen Specter went from R to D in 2009.
These rural Democrat and Republican voters have a message for Washington
The last Democrat elected to the Senate from Texas was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988. He resigned to be in President Bill Clinton’s Cabinet. 1988, coincidentally, is the last year California elected a Republican. It does not feel close — or not as close as Texas — to electing someone from the out-of-power party, but things are changing all the time.
Both Dakotas and Montana were represented by two Democrats within the last 25 years. Now all three are represented by two Republicans, although this year in Montana and South Dakota it is independents, not even Democrats, who are mounting the biggest challenge to Republicans.
The independent who seems to have the best chance of winning at the moment is in Nebraska, where Dan Osborn is challenging Sen. Pete Ricketts. A Democrat last won in Nebraska in 2006.
There are a lot of reasons that running as an independent is tricky in American politics, especially at the state or national level. Osborn’s success might not turn into a Senate seat, but it is a clear message that there are states where party brands are so badly damaged that shedding them could be the best path to unseating an entrenched in-party power. But it’s also true that as the parties change and shift, tectonic moves mean their time in power is ultimately limited.

articles.title_orig: Trump Announces White House Inquiry Into Fed Governor Lisa Cook
articles.title_zh: Trump Announces White House Inquiry Into Fed Governor Lisa Cook
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump opened another chapter in his effort to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook Friday by establishing a "committee of inquiry" to investigate allegations that she made false statements in mortgage applications.
The inquiry will include a hearing at the White House Nov. 5, Trump said in a written memo , that Cook "shall" attend to answer questions from the committee. The hearing wouldn't be public but a transcript would be published, the memo said.
Trump's extraordinary demand that Cook testify before the committee will likely renew concerns about threats to the Federal Reserve's independence. The president has repeatedly called for the central bank to cut its key interest rate, but just last month, the Fed raised it instead , led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, whom Trump appointed earlier this year.
Trump's attempts to fire Cook from the Fed's seven-member board of governors represent the first time in the central bank's 113-year history that a president has sought to remove a Fed governor. Cook was appointed by former President Joe Biden and is the first Black woman on the Fed's board. Trump's attacks on her followed other efforts to oust or indict Black officials , such as New York Attorney General Letitia James and Gen. Charles Q. Brown, the former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
"As President, it is my job to ensure the laws are faithfully executed, including by firing subordinates who cannot be trusted to tell the truth and follow the law," Trump wrote in the memorandum.
Cook's attorneys, Abbe Lowell and Norman Eisen, said they were considering having Cook appear at the Nov. 5 hearing and respond to the charges.
"We have engaged with the White House to evaluate whether the process proposed has a possibility of being a genuine one and not simply a box checking exercise," Lowell and Eisen said in a statement. "Governor Cook welcomes the opportunity to present the facts so she can clear her name and demonstrate there is no legal basis to fire her."
The "committee of inquiry" will be composed of Kevin Hassett, the president's top economic adviser, who has frequently echoed Trump's criticisms of the Fed; Keith Sonderling, the acting director of the Office of Government Ethics, whom the president has also appointed to lead the Labor Department, and Andrea Lucas, the chair of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, whom Trump appointed in November 2025.
Trump initially tried to fire Cook in August 2025 after alleging she had committed mortgage fraud by declaring two different properties to be her "primary" residence in mortgage applications in 2021. Mortgages on primary homes can often receive a lower interest rate or other beneficial terms.
Cook has denied any wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime. Lowell and Eisen have previously said Cook committed an "inadvertent error" and did refer to one of the properties as a vacation home in other documents.
"An inadvertent error is not fraud, as the President and a third of his cabinet should know because they reportedly did the same thing," Lowell and Eisen said in August.
The Federal Reserve declined to comment on Trump's announcement.
Trump and some of his economic advisers have blamed the Fed's broader rate-setting committee, which includes 12 voting members and 19 officials in total, for forcing last month's rate hike, even though it followed comments by Warsh in August that signaled higher rates were likely. As a member of the board of governors, Cook is also one of the 12 voting members of the committee. The vote to lift rates Sept. 16 was unanimous .
The move also follows a Supreme Court ruling in June that Cook could keep her job after Trump sought to fire her last year. That ruling included a footnote that said nothing prevented Trump from "trying again" as long as she was given proper notice and an opportunity to respond to the charges.
Trump said the committee of inquiry will seek to establish whether there is "cause" to fire Cook, as required under the law governing the Fed. The Supreme Court said in June that a for-cause firing required an alleged offense that was serious and related to an official's job.
Scott Alvarez, formerly the chief counsel for the Fed, said that President William Howard Taft set up a similar commission in 1912 to remove two officials from an independent agency. The commission created by Trump goes beyond the type of process the Supreme Court said was needed to fire Cook.
"It's an attempt to show that he's really giving Cook as much process as possible," Alvarez said.
Still, the allegations against Cook don't appear to meet the "for cause" standard set out by the Supreme Court, Alvarez said.
Other analysts said that Trump will likely use the process to ultimately fire Cook.
"We do not see why the White House would start this process if it were not trying to create a way to justify removing Cook from her job," Jaret Seiberg, managing director of TD Cowen's Washington Research Group, said in a note to clients.

articles.title_orig: Trump lifts sanctions on Russian diesel, suggests US may buy amid surging fuel prices
articles.title_zh: Trump lifts sanctions on Russian diesel, suggests US may buy amid surging fuel prices
articles.content_orig:
US President Donald Trump says he has reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin allowing Moscow to "immediately release" diesel into the global market.
He said Putin had agreed to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another million after that.
"Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!" Trump wrote on Truth social.
An envoy to Putin welcomed the deal, but Ukraine's president said any easing of sanctions on Russia played into Moscow's hands and would prolong a war that must be ended.
Diesel prices in the US have doubled since the war with Iran began in February, putting pressure on Republicans ahead of the midterm elections over the rising cost of living.
The average diesel price in the US is currently $6.28 a gallon, according to the AAA, down from the record high of $6.53 recorded at the the end of September.
Shortly after Trump's announcement, the US Treasury formally issued a temporary license allowing Russian diesel into the market.
An envoy for Putin, Kirill Dmitriev, welcomed the deal on social media, saying: "Russia-US co-operation on diesel and energy will benefit the world."
But Volodymyr Zelensky hit out at the deal, saying "gifts to Putin will not work for peace" and that Russia would repay the diesel with "further terror".
"Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged," he wrote on social media.
This year Russia has experienced two waves of severe fuel shortages across the country as a result of Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries.
According to the International Energy Agency, its diesel production is estimated to have fallen by nearly 30%.
Trump has expressed his displeasure over those attacks, blaming them for rising fuel prices.
But on Friday Zelensky defended the strikes, saying there were in response to "Russia's years-long campaign of terror against Ukraine's energy sector".
"Ukraine will not set Russian oil refineries on fire if Russia does not destroy our energy infrastructure," he said.
Trump's announced deal represents a remarkable about-face, as the US Congress recently enacted legislation - signed by the president - to authorise new American sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas.
The president's Truth Social posts often provide incomplete information. The details of exactly how Russia is supplying this fuel to the global market, and what they might get for in return is unclear.
It opens Trump up to criticism from European allies and pro-Ukraine politicians in the US, that the American president is now helping to fund the Russian war machine.
What impact the deal with Russia will have on fuel prices also remains unclear. The global benchmark for crude oil, Brent, remains above $103 a barrel. Before the war with Iran, Brent crude was trading at about $73 a barrel.
The BBC has contacted the White House for comment on what reimbursement the US is providing Russia in return for the release of diesel.
It is the latest effort from the president to lower fuel prices in the US, as he has spent months grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war and its impact on global energy prices.
That conflict has sent the cost of petrol and, in particular diesel, skyrocketing in America in recent months, which has soured his standing with the public who have been stung by the higher pump prices and knock-on effects that led to across-the board inflation.
With the looming midterm congressional elections - which will determine if Republicans maintain control of Congress - the American president has been searching for ways to ease his party's political pain.
Earlier this week, Trump said he was "thinking about" suspending the federal tax on gasoline, and also announced that he would allow so-called red dye diesel to be used on US highways without facing federal tax.
He has also successfully pressured G7 nations into releasing 100 million barrels of oil and diesel from stockpiles to help ease supply concerns, and previously supported calls for a ban on diesel exports from the US.

articles.content_orig:
WEST GROVE, Pa. (WPVI) -- The Chester County Health Department is warning the public of a possible measles exposure at several local stores.
The possible exposure happened on Sunday, Oct. 4, at the following locations:
-CVS at 870 Baltimore Pike, Kennett Square, 19348; between 10:45 a.m. and 3 p.m.
-CVS at 857 West Baltimore Pike, West Grove, 19390; between 12:30 p.m. and 3:30 p.m.
-Giant at 849 Baltimore Pike, West Grove, 19390; between 1 p.m. and 3:45 p.m.
A person infected with measles visited those locations while contagious, county health officials said.
RELATED: Measles cases surpass 1,000 in Pennsylvania amid the state's largest outbreak in decades
Anyone at those locations is urged to check whether they are immune to measles.
The health department said you are considered immune against measles if any of the following apply to you:
-Have already had measles, or
-Have received at least one of the two doses of measles-containing vaccine (usually given as measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine).
People who aren't protected against measles can get the virus up to two hours after someone with measles left the same room or airspace, health officials said.
This incident comes amid a historic measles outbreaking Pennsylvania, with more than 1,000 cases reported.

articles.title_orig: Human Rights Lawyer Navi Pillay Is Awarded Nobel Peace Prize
articles.title_zh: Human Rights Lawyer Navi Pillay Is Awarded Nobel Peace Prize
articles.content_orig:
South African judge Navanethem “Navi” Pillay has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, becoming the fifth South African to win it.
Making the announcement on Friday, the Norwegian Nobel Committee praised Pillay for her decades-long efforts to prosecute genocide and war crimes, which have been marked by “judicial rigour, personal integrity and considerable courage”.
From defending activists in apartheid-era South Africa, to more recently overseeing a United Nations inquiry which declared Israel responsible for genocide in Gaza, the 85-year-old, who is also a judge at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), has specialised in international law for decades.
Here’s what we know about her life and why she has been awarded the world’s top peace prize:
Navanethem Pillay, known as Navi Pillay, was born in the racially segregated city of Durban in South Africa’s Natal province in 1940 to parents of Tamil descent.
After earning a law degree from the University of Natal, she became the first woman in Natal province to start her own law firm. Early in her career, she helped defend numerous anti-apartheid activists in the country.
She later became the first woman of colour to sit on the High Court of South Africa. She went on to preside over the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR), which prosecuted those charged with humanitarian crimes during the 1994 Rwandan genocide .
Pillay was the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) from 2008 to 2014. More recently she chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory which determined last year that Israel is responsible for carrying out genocide in Gaza .
Currently, Pillay is a judge on the International Court of Justice, acting in a case in which Myanmar is accused of genocide against its mostly Muslim Rohingya minority.
Pillay has spent much of her life advocating for human rights in her home South Africa and abroad. While studying, she took part in boycotts and marches against apartheid. She later joined the legal defence of some of the country’s most prominent anti-apartheid figures, such as Phyllis Naidoo and Strini Moodley.
In 1973, Pillay took on a case that helped secure basic rights, including legal access, for political prisoners on Robben Island, where Nelson Mandela was jailed.
In a 2016 interview with the Diplomatic Courier, Pillay said her early human rights work was “shaped by what (she) had experienced under apartheid”.
“I used many of the challenges to my advantage, I had to learn international humanitarian law so as to defend cases of racial discrimination,” she said.
Pillay oversaw a UN commission of inquiry which concluded in 2025 that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.
In a statement on the report, Pillay urged UN member states to do everything they can to establish a ceasefire in Gaza and to “ensure justice and accountability for all victims”.
The Nobel committee said Pillay was being honoured for her “efforts to promote peace and international law”.
It called her one of “the great defenders of international legal principles in our time”, having helped hold states and national leaders to account and bring “hope to victims of violence and conflict”.
The committee stressed the role Pillay played in the Rwandan genocide tribunal, saying her influence helped establish “that rape and sexual violence could constitute a crime against humanity – as well as genocide”.
“In the same case, Ms Pillay was instrumental in a separate legal breakthrough: for the first time, a defendant faced charges of incitement to commit genocide purely on the basis of spreading propaganda,” said the committee.
The committee said honouring Pillay is especially important at a time when international law “is under tremendous pressure and its institutions are under attack”.
That message was echoed by rights advocates and international officials.
The UN’s rights chief, Volker Turk, said her award was “a recognition, a reaffirmation that human rights, the rule of law and justice and accountability are fundamental to everything, to peace, to security and prosperity”.
International Criminal Court (ICC) President Tomoko Akane said the award carried special significance “at a time of profound challenges to the international legal order and the rule of law”.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa praised the award as a tribute to Pillay’s “courage, integrity ⁠⁠⁠⁠and lifelong commitment to justice”.
Haakon Gjerlow, acting director of the Peace Research Institute Oslo, said it “sends a clear message that peace depends not only on political leadership, but on strong, credible international institutions and the courageous people who dedicate their lives to defending them .”
Ashok Swain, a professor of peace and conflict research at Uppsala University, told Al Jazeera that the selection of Pillay was a “pleasant surprise” and the “best possible choice”.
He said the Nobel committee likely took into consideration Pillay’s lifelong record fighting genocide and apartheid. He added that the award to the South African jurist could also be read as a message to United States President Donald Trump, who has long argued that he is deserving of the peace prize and whose administration has clashed with South Africa over debunked claims that white Afrikaners are facing “genocide” .
Furthermore, last year, the Trump administration issued sanctions against members of the ICC in what many critics saw as an attack on the system of international law.
The ICC had previously issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity.
The ICC responded by describing the US sanctions as a “flagrant attack against the independence of an impartial judicial institution” and the victims of war crimes around the world. It said it would continue its work “without regard to any restriction, pressure or threat”.
Pillay appeared to learn of the award as media reports circulated, telling a group of supporters applauding her: “I don’t know about this. So my question is: Is it true?”
She also jokingly referenced Trump, saying, “If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump.”
Once the news was confirmed, Pillay said she would dedicate the award to “all of the survivors of international crimes”.
“This award strengthens my conviction that we must ⁠⁠⁠⁠stand together in defence of ⁠⁠⁠⁠the rule of law, in defence of independent ⁠⁠⁠⁠courts and an international ⁠⁠⁠⁠legal order based ⁠⁠⁠⁠on principle.”
Earlier, the Nobel committee said it had struggled to get in touch with Pillay to notify her. “If you see a Norwegian number calling, please pick up,” said committee chair, Jorgen Watne Frydnes.

articles.title_orig: The Brit coaching the world’s game
articles.title_zh: The Brit coaching the world’s game
articles.content_orig:
Central Michigan University soccer head coach James Decosmo looks back at his staff before the game at the Soccer/Lacrosse Complex on Thursday, Sept. 17, 2026. (CM-Life | Jasmine Brookins)
James Decosemo flew from the United Kingdom to the United States more than a decade ago to be a college student, with aspirations of a future in soccer.
Now, he is the head coach of the Central Michigan University women’s soccer team, the sport he has followed his whole life.
“I’m lucky that I get to do it my whole life because it really is my whole life,” Decosemo said.
The James from St. James Park
Decosemo was raised a Newcastle United fan in Stokesley, England and became a season ticket holder at age eight. Even with Newcastle having only won one major trophy in recent history, he fell in love with the sport of soccer because of the Magpies.
In addition to watching legends like Alan Shearer weekly, Decosemo took interest in the manager, Sir Bobby Robson, who also managed Barcelona and the English national team.
“I think he’s a master of man management,” Decosemo said. “I’d love to get to a point where I’m a master of man management.”
Newcastle won its first major competition just a year and a half ago, winning the Carabao Cup 2-1 in 2025 against Liverpool. Decosemo said it is one of the reasons why he loves soccer so much.
“That was an unbelievable moment,” he said. “They hadn’t won one (trophy), obviously in my lifetime, but also in my dad’s lifetime.”
Although his passion ran deep for the Magpies, Decosemo was presented with an opportunity to leave the country to continue to play soccer.
“They introduced us through that process to the opportunity to come to the States to play, which got me really excited,” he said.
The now-Chippewas manager would leave England to go across the pond and into the mitten, attending and playing soccer for Northwood University in Midland, MI.
Since moving to the United States, he’s only been back to St. James Park a handful of times to support Newcastle, but every time has been memorable for Decosemo.
“I went back and watched us play AC Milan in the Champions League, which was awesome,” he said. “If we won, we’d have gone through to the Champions League (knockout stages). If AC Milan win, then they go through ... both teams just going at it.”
Decosemo said that this was the last time he had been back home.
Decosemo met his wife at Northwood. After graduating in 2016, he started his coaching career in Michigan to stay near his wife’s family and the connections he made.
“Probably in all worlds, but soccer especially, there’s a lot of getting jobs through people,” Decosemo said.
Coaching in the US showed him the differences compared to the UK, mainly the rules and the athleticism of the players.
“I think generally, it’s known that the US is more athletic,” he said. “It’s bigger, faster, stronger and the game’s played that way.”
The rule that was so different to him was about substitution. In European soccer, if a player is subbed off, they cannot come back on the pitch later in the game. However, in college soccer, players can come back. The rule changes the pace of the game, ridding the match of lulls, according to Decosemo.
“The game never really changes speed,” he said. “That’s something that definitely I had to adapt to as a player for sure and then as a coach, just knowing that it’s probably a more squad game here than it is other places.”
His first job was at Saginaw Valley State University as a coach for the women’s team, but it wasn’t until his head-coaching job for the women’s team at Aquinas University, that Decosemo was introduced to the difference compared to the men’s game.
“I think the women’s game is probably a little bit more tactical,” he said. “The coach has a little bit more influence in the moment and that’s the way I played and that’s the way I coached.”
Decosemo was the head coach for the Aquinas women’s team from 2022 to 2025. In that span, he recorded a 55-5-7 overall record, with an undefeated 31-0-3 record in the Wolverine Hoosier Athletic Conference. In addition to winning the games, he also won trophies, with five conference championships, with three won in the regular season.
Last year, he made the jump to the NCAA and Division I, going to Kalamazoo to be an assistant coach for Western Michigan’s women’s team. The Broncos went undefeated in the Mid-American Conference, winning both the regular season and post-season competitions, while also beating the Chippewas 3-1.
After the Chippewas let go of their previous head coach last November, Athletic Director Amy Folan called Decosemo about taking the vacant spot a month later.
“When I got the phone call, everything was about trying to win,” he said. “A lot of these jobs, especially in women’s soccer, is just be successful, have a good environment, make sure that the students graduate, which, of course, are important that those things still have to happen here. But the drive to be successful on the field was what I wanted because that’s what I want to do.”
For a manager coming into a new team, it can take a while to adjust the culture and playing style, especially with most of the squad returning. With the team only winning one game last season, the shift was imminent.
“I got to just start with who I am and who we’re going to be rather than maybe navigating to it over a longer period of time,” Decosemo said. “I purposely didn’t ask too much about the previous program and how it was ran. I just went in with what we’re going to do.”
The one collaboration he made with the old program was with assistant coach Keyton Wheelock, who has been at CMU since January 2021.
“We talked a lot about philosophies and the direction he wanted to take the program, and I bought in,” Wheelock said. “I believed in what he was saying and I believed he could make the changes that he said he could make.”
Not only are the returning coaches buying in, the players are also seeing the change.
Rachel Jackson is a senior who earned academic all-conference in 2024 and a team captain in 2025.
“I think we’ve been prepped really well each game knowing what the opponent’s going to do, but always staying true to how we’re going to go with our shape with our attack, with our belief,” Jackson said. “I think we’ve just all been together on the same page from the start of the game to the end of the game.”
Jackson plays a role that is usually referred to as a wingback, where she plays up and down her side of the field. Decosemo said she is the most consistent player on the team and is one of the most impactful.
“The difference probably between Rachel and arguably the rest is that her lows haven’t been noticeable,” Decosemo said. “She’s had some really good moments too, got a game-winning goal in our first win and really contributed in big moments.”
Her game-winning goal was against Charleston Southern University in the second game of the season. Decosemo said the win has been one of his most cherished moments at CMU so far.
“That’s the big standout moment, getting that first win as a group and seeing them celebrate and even hearing the comments say, ‘We don’t know what to do. We’ve won a game,’” he said.
As a manager, the Englishman picks the formation and tactics based on the players on the team. He’s had previous success with the 3-5-2, which also fits the Chippewas’ squad the best. The tactic has three defenders, five midfielders and two strikers. With an overflow of midfielders, the wingers play all over their side of the field.
“The reason that we have wing backs is in my style, our style, the wide players that we have suit that role,” Decosemo said. “They’re physically pretty good at covering ground, but they’re not super crafty or creative in terms of the way they attack, so they’re great at covering, coming from deep and maybe crossing from deep or whatever it is.”

articles.title_orig: Join in a Salem400+ World Record Attempt at 'Witch Hats on the Wharf'
articles.title_zh: Join in a Salem400+ World Record Attempt at 'Witch Hats on the Wharf'
articles.content_orig:
Haunted Happenings has once again returned to Salem this October with a month of signature events, family activities, live entertainment, and Halloween festivities throughout the city. This year’s celebration takes on added significance as Salem marks its 400th anniversary. The City of Salem and Salem400+ have been marking this milestone year with parades, parties, fun events, park and infrastructure improvements, and this month, in a nod toward Salem’s iconic annual Haunted Happenings celebrations, a special attempt to make history with a world record attempt , as hundreds (or even thousands) of people wearing witch hats gather in the park along the city’s historic waterfront. Whether you’re a local, a longtime Haunted Happenings fan, or visiting Salem for the first time, this is your chance to be part of a 400th anniversary moment. Come for the record. Stay for the waterfront, the shops, the restaurants, & the full Salem experience.
Community members interested in participating should plan to don their favorite witch hat of any size, style or color and head to Salem Maritime National Historical Park (160 Derby Street, Salem) on Saturday, October 17, 2026 before 11:00am . History making photos of the assembled crowd will be taken from overhead at and shortly after 11:00am. As many road closures will be in place throughout downtown due to large anticipated weekend crowds, participants should avoid driving to the park, expect significant foot traffic throughout downtown at that time, and plan to allow for extra time in order to make their way to the event.
One of the world’s largest Halloween celebrations, Salem Haunted Happenings draws more than 1 million visitors from around the globe for a uniquely Salem blend of history, culture, creativity, and Halloween fun. This year, festivities formally kicked off October 1 with the traditional Salem Chamber of Commerce Haunted Happenings Grand Parade and will continue throughout the month, this year culminating on Halloween night with a spectacular 400-drone show commemorating Salem’s 400th anniversary.
“October is a time when Salem's history, creativity, and community spirit are on especially on full display,” remarked Mayor Dominick Pangallo , “While we’ve been marking Salem400+ throughout 2026 in many ways, from signature parks and infrastructure improvements, to parades, parties and historic lectures, and honoring volunteerism and special community members and more, this year’s Haunted Happenings festivities need a commemorative Salem 400+ moment as well, and we're excited to take the opportunity during this busy time of the year for a history-making photo capturing the excitement in Salem at this time of year. The Witch Hats on the Wharf event is a fun opportunity for people to be part of Salem400+ history, and I encourage community members to walk down to Derby Wharf to join in the fun. I’m grateful to Destination Salem, Salem Maritime National Historical Park Services, and City of Salem staff for making this fun event possible, and I'm especially proud that the commemorative witch hat campaign will also support HAWC and its vital work serving survivors and families throughout our region.”
“We’re especially excited for this year’s Salem Haunted Happenings as we celebrate Salem’s 400th anniversary and welcome visitors from around the world to experience everything that makes October in Salem so special,” said Ashley Judge, Executive Director of Destination Salem . “One of the highlights will be Witch Hats on the Wharf , when we invite residents and visitors to fill Derby Wharf with witch hats for an unforgettable community photo and world record attempt. It’s a fun and uniquely Salem way to bring everyone together and make a little history during this milestone year.”
Along with this event, the City of Salem is selling limited-edition Salem 400+ branded witch hats and patches at the Witch House, Charter Street Cemetery, and Old Town Hall - while supplies last. Hats are $30 and patches are $7. All proceeds will be donated to HAWC (Healing Abuse, Working for Change), a Salem-based nonprofit that has spent over four decades providing free, trauma-informed services to survivors of domestic abuse across 23 cities and towns on Massachusetts' North Shore. The special-edition hats and patches feature the Salem 400+ logo in HAWC's signature purple and orange colors.

articles.title_orig: China and Europe Step Back From Trade War With Limits on Chinese Car Exports
articles.title_zh: China and Europe Step Back From Trade War With Limits on Chinese Car Exports
articles.content_orig:
The agreement will see Chinese hybrid vehicle exports decline by ‘several million cars’ in the coming years, EU trade chief says
The European Union and China have “reached an understanding” that will cut Chinese hybrid car shipments to the bloc by “more than a half”, in a temporary salve to trade tensions that have threatened to boil over into a full-blown trade war.
Speaking after marathon trade talks in Beijing, EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic said the deal would see China slash its hybrid car exports “by several million cars” over a four-year period.
“This is the first time that China has accepted to moderate its exports without going through the phase of prior trade tensions, and I very much appreciate that,” Sefcovic told reporters in the Chinese capital.
The sides also agreed to expedite EU applications for rare earth mineral export licences and improve market access for goods including car parts, olive oil and textiles, which Sefcovic said could be worth “almost €4 billion” (US$4.5 billion) in current export value.

articles.content_orig:
Cookies allow us to understand how you use this site and improve your experience. Our detailed Cookie Policy can be found here . By continuing to use this website you accept our use of cookies.
Mandatory cookies help make this website usable by enabling basic functions like page navigation and access to secure areas of the website. Our website cannot function properly without these cookies.
Statistic cookies help us understand how visitors interact with this website, for example seeing which pages are most popular. This information is collected anonymously and helps us improve the site by making the most sought after information easy to find.
Marketing cookies are used to track visitors across websites allowing the display of ads that are relevant and engaging for the visitor. Whilst we do not display any advertising on the WJC website, allowing marketing cooking may allow other sites to see that you have visited our site.
Amb. Lauder Calls Pillay’s Selection “A Shocking Affront to Those Who Oppose Antisemitism”
NEW YORK – After the Norwegian Nobel Committee announced that South African jurist Navi Pillay will receive the Nobel Peace Prize 2026, Amb. Ronald S. Lauder, president of the World Jewish Congress, released the following statement:
“Navi Pillay is no diplomat and certainly no peacemaker. The Norwegian Nobel Committee’s decision to award her the Peace Prize is a shocking affront to those who oppose antisemitism and defend Jewish life everywhere.
“We reject Pillay’s accusations of genocide against Israel as baseless, politically motivated, and unsupported by credible evidence. She has lent the UN’s authority to a campaign that demonizes the Jewish state and fuels hostility toward Jews worldwide. The biased process she has led has brought shame upon the United Nations and undermined its credibility.
“Jewish communities repeatedly challenged her conduct and called for her removal. The committee has chosen to reward conduct that should have warranted her dismissal. That decision discredits the Peace Prize itself.”

articles.title_orig: 7.6 earthquake strikes Panama
articles.title_zh: 7.6 earthquake strikes Panama
articles.content_orig:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck off Panama's southern coast Friday, shaking the country's capital as officials investigated a potential tsunami threat.
The U.S. Geological Survey initially measured the earthquake at magnitude 8.0 before lowering its estimate to 7.7. The quake struck at 1:56 p.m. ET, approximately 6 miles beneath the surface, near Pitaloza Arriba, Panama. A 5.5 magnitude aftershock followed, with its epicenter approximately 50 miles east of the initial earthquake.
MORE THAN 3,000 MISSING AFTER COLOMBIA EARTHQUAKE AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROVIDES $15.5 MILLION IN RELIEF
People stand outside the maternity ward of the Santo Tomas hospital, following a severe magnitude 8 earthquake thet hit the country, in Panama City on October 9, 2026. (Photo by Martin Bernetti/AFP via Getty Images)
The earthquake was felt in Panama City and in San José, the capital of neighboring Costa Rica, according to Reuters.
Tsunami officials warned that waves reaching 3 to 10 feet above tide levels were possible along some coastal areas of Panama, while parts of Ecuador could experience waves of approximately 1 to 3 feet.
Smaller tsunami waves of less than 1 foot above tide levels were forecast for coastal areas of Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Mexico, Nicaragua and Peru.
COLOMBIA BUILDING COLLAPSES ON CAMERA AS EARTHQUAKE BRINGS DEATH, DESTRUCTION
Medical workers and patients gather outside a hospital following a powerful earthquake in Panama on Oct. 9, 2026. (Photo by Martin Bernetti/AFP via Getty Images)
Despite the potential danger to coastal communities near the earthquake, officials said a Pacific-wide tsunami was not expected.
Earthquakes measuring between 7.0 and 7.9 can cause serious damage, according to Michigan Technological University .
Information about possible damage or casualties from Friday's earthquake was not immediately available.
People gather in a Panama City square after evacuating a building following a powerful earthquake. (Arnulfo Franco/AFP via Getty Images)

articles.title_orig: Top Democratic Group Pumps Millions Into Kansas Senate Race
articles.title_zh: Top Democratic Group Pumps Millions Into Kansas Senate Race
articles.content_orig:
Democrats are dreaming of a revolution in Kansas in November, trying to believe in polling that shows a tight race in the Senate contest there between the Democrat, Rev. Adam Hamilton, and the Republican incumbent, Sen. Roger Marshall.
It would indeed be a watershed moment if Hamilton takes the seat: No Democrat has won a Senate seat in Kansas since 1932, not quite a century but a very, very long time.
In fact, since Kansas became a state in 1861, only three Democrats have represented it in the Senate. It’s a remarkable statistic since the two parties have evolved so much during that time.
Related: Read a Q and A with a Kansas-based political expert from CNN’s What Matters newsletter about why Kansas has stayed Republican at the Senate level for so long and why Kansans feel targeted by some of Trump’s policies this year.
While American politics seem locked in place; 30 of the 50 states have been represented by a senator from both parties during this century. And while the states that have been represented by both parties most recently track closely with the swing states that decide elections, there are a few exceptions, like Montana and Alabama.
No Republican has been elected to represent the islands since 1970. That Republican, Hiram Fong, was one of Hawaii’s two first senators, elected when Hawaii became a state in 1959. No Democrat has been elected to represent Wyoming or Utah since that same year.
The longest streak east of the Mississippi River is in New Jersey, where no Republican has been elected to the US Senate since Clifford Case was elected in 1972, capping a long career on Capitol Hill. A Republican senator, Jeffrey Chiesa, was briefly appointed to serve in 2013. That was the result of the state having a Republican governor, Chris Christie, at the time.
The Senate is up for grabs. Plot each party’s best path to winning
A Kansas voter would have to be well over 100 years old to have voted for the state’s last Democratic senator, but the current governor is a Democrat.
In New Hampshire, the state is represented by two Democratic senators. The last Republican elected was Kelly Ayotte in 2010. She’s currently the state’s governor. And Republicans hope that another former senator, John Sununu, can break the trend and reclaim a Senate seat this year. When he served as senator, the state had two Republican senators.
Far fewer states are sending a split delegation — both a Republican and a Democratic senator — than ever before in US history. Since the nationwide election of senators began with the 1914 election after the ratification of the 17th amendment, there have generally been at least 10 and frequently more than 20 split delegations, according to a 2021 analysis by Pew .
Currently there are only four: Vermont, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin — none of which has a Senate race this year — and Maine, where Republican Sen. Susan Collins is among the most endangered incumbents. If she loses to Democrat Troy Jackson, Maine will join the wave of states bringing their senators in line with their status as blue or red for presidential purposes. And Collins is one of the few true moderates of either party left in the chamber.
The other senator from Maine, Angus King, is an independent, but like Sen. Bernie Sanders in Vermont, he sides with Democrats in procedural matters, making him a Democrat for purposes of determining which party controls the Senate.
The last time Vermont elected a Republican, Sen. Jim Jeffords in 2000, he ended up switching parties when Republicans angered him. There’s conjecture now that Pennsylvania’s Democratic Sen. John Fetterman might soon do the inverse, but he has insisted that he will remain a Democrat.
There’s Pennsylvania precedent for party-switching. Sen. Arlen Specter went from R to D in 2009.
These rural Democrat and Republican voters have a message for Washington
The last Democrat elected to the Senate from Texas was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988. He resigned to be in President Bill Clinton’s Cabinet. 1988, coincidentally, is the last year California elected a Republican. It does not feel close — or not as close as Texas — to electing someone from the out-of-power party, but things are changing all the time.
Both Dakotas and Montana were represented by two Democrats within the last 25 years. Now all three are represented by two Republicans, although this year in Montana and South Dakota it is independents, not even Democrats, who are mounting the biggest challenge to Republicans.
The independent who seems to have the best chance of winning at the moment is in Nebraska, where Dan Osborn is challenging Sen. Pete Ricketts. A Democrat last won in Nebraska in 2006.
There are a lot of reasons that running as an independent is tricky in American politics, especially at the state or national level. Osborn’s success might not turn into a Senate seat, but it is a clear message that there are states where party brands are so badly damaged that shedding them could be the best path to unseating an entrenched in-party power. But it’s also true that as the parties change and shift, tectonic moves mean their time in power is ultimately limited.

articles.title_orig: Class action alleges Webull misled investors about China operations
articles.title_zh: Class action alleges Webull misled investors about China operations
articles.content_orig:
A class action accuses Webull of hiding the real scale of its China operations from investors.
A securities complaint filed October 8 in federal court in Tampa, Florida, alleges online broker-dealer Webull Corporation told investors one story about its ties to mainland China while the reality, according to the filing, was very different.
The complaint, Ward v. Webull Corporation et al. (Case No. 8:26-cv-03052), brings claims under federal securities laws - specifically Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act and SEC Rule 10b-5. It names Webull - a Cayman Islands-incorporated broker-dealer whose shares trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker "BULL" - along with the company's founder and CEO, and its CFO, as defendants.
The company describes itself as a broker-dealer regulated in 12 major markets globally, with US offices in St. Petersburg, Florida.
The case centers on a string of SEC filings the complaint alleges painted an incomplete picture. In its 2024 annual report, a July 2025 registration statement, and its 2025 annual report, Webull told investors its "operations in mainland China are limited to research and development and technical support functions," according to the complaint. Those filings also stated that US customer data "cannot be transmitted outside of the United States or accessed by our non-U.S. employees without permission and oversight from our U.S. personnel."
The complaint alleges those statements were "false and/or misleading." In reality, the filing claims, "Webull's core platform, software development, data pipelines, and core engineering depended on PRC-based personnel and on technology infrastructure subject to Chinese law."
More broadly, the complaint alleges that "Webull's ownership structure, technical workforce, technology infrastructure, cross-border data routing, financing, and compliance structure were structurally tied to China" - contradicting the company's assurances that its main business operations were US-based.
The numbers in Webull's own filings tell the story. The complaint points to the company's July 2025 registration statement, which disclosed that its mainland China subsidiary, Hunan Weibu Information Technology Co., Ltd., "employs 731 employees, representing 61% of our employees as of December 31, 2024." By the end of 2025, the complaint alleges, that figure had climbed to 863 employees - 62% of Webull's global workforce.
The complaint also alleges that the US House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party delivered a letter to the CEO of Webull Financial - the company's US broker-dealer arm - in December 2024, seeking information about the relationship between Webull Financial and Webull's China operations, and about the security of customer data.
According to the complaint, Webull's SEC filings characterized the Select Committee's concerns as "largely based on outdated and inaccurate information."
That position became harder to hold on October 7, 2026. The complaint alleges that before markets opened, CNBC reported the Select Committee had found a "profound gap" between how Webull presented itself as an American company and its actual control and operations. The committee also reportedly found that Webull "initially told the Select Committee that it had no offices or employees in China," the complaint alleges.
Webull's stock dropped sharply. The complaint alleges the company's Class A ordinary shares fell $1.39 per share - approximately 19% - to close at $5.89 on unusually heavy trading volume.
The complaint alleges the company's founder and CEO - a citizen of the People's Republic of China who, as of March 31, 2026, held approximately 79.2% of total voting power - "knew or recklessly disregarded" the extent of Webull's dependence on China-based operations.
For advisors and compliance teams, this complaint is worth watching. The allegations raise questions about due diligence on broker-dealer platforms with complex cross-border structures - and about what happens when a company's SEC filings and a congressional investigation tell different stories about where operations actually sit.
The allegations in this complaint have not been tested in court. No court has ruled on the merits of the case.

articles.title_orig: Nitrogen leads solid Casse quartet at Breeders’ Cup World Championships
articles.title_zh: Nitrogen leads solid Casse quartet at Breeders’ Cup World Championships
articles.content_orig:
D.J. Stable’s Kentucky homebred Nitrogen will make her third appearance at the Breeders’ Cup World Championships when she headlines a talented field in the Grade 1, $2 million Breeders’ Cup Distaff.
Trained by dual Hall of Famer Mark Casse, the 4-year-old Medaglia d’Oro bay made her last three outings in New York, including a pair of memorable Grade 1 starts at Saratoga Race Course with a 12 3/4-length romp in the Ogden Phipps presented by Ford and a runner-up effort to reigning Horse of the Year Sovereignty while facing males in the Whitney.
Her Ogden Phipps effort earned a career-best 113 Beyer Speed Figure with the Chad Brown-trained runner-up Fully Subscribed exiting that race to win three graded events, including a pair of Grade 1s.
Nitrogen had her final Breeders’ Cup prep at Belmont Park, wiring a field of five to score by 2 3/4-lengths under regular rider Jose Ortiz in the Grade 2 Beldame on September 25.
“We shipped her down to Kentucky on Wednesday and she trained this morning at Keeneland. She's doing well,” Casse said. “I thought the Beldame was a good race. I liked the timing. It looks like a showdown between her and Chad's filly.”
Casse said he has no intention of dulling Nitrogen’s abundant early foot in a Distaff field expected to have other potential pace types.
“She'll be pretty close. We may slow her down a little bit but we're not going to take hold of her. We're going to let her do her thing,” Casse said.
Nitrogen has banked in excess of $3 million through an 18-9-6-3 record that includes a trio of graded wins on turf and five graded wins on dirt. Her previous Breeders’ Cup attempts came at Del Mar, including a closing third as a maiden in the 2024 Grade 1 Juvenile Fillies Turf and a runner-up try to Scylla in last year’s Distaff.
While Casse hopes she can go one better in the Distaff at Keeneland, he’s buoyed by the fact that D. J. Stable plans to bring back the reigning Champion 3-Year-Old Filly for another season of racing next year.
“That's the plan as long as she's healthy out of the Breeders' Cup,” Casse said. “Our sport needs its stars and she's definitely a star. I commend the Greens for being the sportsmen they are.”
Gary Barber, Bridlewood Farm and Eclipse Thoroughbred Partners’ late-running Measure has hit the board in each of her last four outings – the last three in Grade 1 company – and will look to capitalize on a potential pace battle in the Breeders’ Cup Distaff.
The 3-year-old daughter of Essential Quality finished third in the nine-furlong Grade 1 Coaching Club American Oaks won by stablemate Counting Stars in July at Saratoga to begin her streak of top-flight tilts. She followed with a neck second to My Gun's Loaded in the Spa’s 10-furlong Alabama presented by Keeneland Sales on August 22 ahead of a closing third in the 1 1/16-mile Cotillion on September 19 at Parx when in tight approaching the three-eighths.
“She's a filly that we were high on from the beginning. I wasn't that disappointed with her earlier on in the year, I just thought she needed to get her act together and needed some pace,” Casse said. “Her Alabama was a huge race, and she got very unlucky in the Cotillion. She'll enjoy the mile and an eighth and will also enjoy a hot pace, which looking at the Distaff it's looking like it will be fairly lively.”
Manny Franco will retain the mount on Measure.
Gary Barber, Blue Crevalle Racing and Eclipse Thoroughbred Partners’ Classic Q was initially considered for a Breeders’ Cup start versus males in the Grade 1 Mile but will instead target the Grade 1 Filly and Mare Turf.
The 4-year-old Classic Empire grey has won 3-of-6 starts this year, including frontrunning scores in the Grade 2 Distaff Turf Mile in May at Churchill Downs and the Grade 1 Just a Game presented by Resolute Racing on June 6 at Saratoga. She secured her second career Grade 1 last out with a stalking nose score over Lush Lips in the one-mile First Lady on October 3 at Keeneland.
“We thought about the Mile but we're going to run her against the girls,” Casse said. “I would think with the mile and three-sixteenths that more than likely she'll be on the lead.”
Hall of Famer Javier Castellano takes over aboard Classic Q from fellow Hall of Famer John Velazquez, who is committed to Gimma a Nother.
D.J. Stable will also be represented by Voyager in the Grade 1 Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf.
The Justify bay ran second in her first two outings on dirt, including a runner-up try to Harper’s Corner in the Listed Schuylerville on July 3 at the Spa.
Voyager then shifted to the Saratoga turf on August 1 and stretched out to a two-turn 1 1/16-miles to post a frontrunning nose score over Correlation Trade. The third-place finisher of that event, Bittersweet Memory, exited to graduate at Saratoga and followed with a fourth-place run in the Grade 2 Miss Grillo here last weekend.
Voyager enters the Breeders’ Cup from a 1 1/4-length win in the Grade 1 Natalma contested at a one-turn mile over firm E.P. Taylor turf on September 12 at Woodbine.
Casse said the Spa turf experience will be beneficial for Voyager as she goes back to two turns for the one-mile Juvenile Fillies Turf.
“When she broke her maiden at Saratoga, I was happy because we were able to get a two-turn race into her. We went back to one-turn for the Natalma, but I feel she's very versatile. Her race in the Natalma was really good and she's training really well,” Casse said.
Casse enjoyed a winning barn debut Thursday for world-traveler Facteur Cheval , who scored by a half-length under Irad Ortiz, Jr. in a 1 1/16-mile Keeneland allowance for owners Team Valor International and Gary Barber.
The 7-year-old Ribchester gelding has banked in excess of $5.7 million through a 28-7-7-6 ledger topped by a win in the 2024 Group 1 Dubai Turf. He landed a deep-closing sixth in the Grade 3 Mint Millions on September 7 at Kentucky Downs for his former trainer Jerome Reynier.
“We took him over right after that race. Barry [Irwin] had mentioned to us going into yesterday's race that you need to get him into the race,” Casse said. “We let Irad know you need to be aggressive early on with him and get him into the race and you saw that yesterday. It made the difference. It's a privilege to have that horse in the barn.”
Facteur Cheval will point to the Grade 3 River City on November 7 at Churchill Downs.
Casse enjoyed his second win at the new Belmont Park on Wednesday when Gary Barber’s Ori wired a one-mile turf starter optional-claimer in her first start for new connections after being haltered for $45,000 from an optional-claiming win in September at Saratoga.
With Castellano aboard, the 5-year-old Hard Spun chestnut zipped through splits of 22.39 seconds, 45.09 and 1:09.48 en route to a 6 1/4-length score in 1:33.35. The winning effort returned an 86 Beyer – four points shy of a career-best 90 earned from a runner-up try in the 2024 Listed Winter Memories at Belmont at the Big A.
Ori is out of the stakes-winning Pioneerof the Nile mare Princessof the Nyl. Her stakes-winning third dam, Arabis, is a full-sister to multiple graded stakes-winner Atelier and a half-sister to Grade 1-winner Aldiza.
“We don't claim very many. She's unique in that we thought she looked like she had ability running, but we also claimed her to be a broodmare,” Casse said. “If she keeps running the way she ran the other day, she may run another year.
“Javi called me after the race and said, 'she was impressive.' Normally I call him, but he called me,” Casse added, with a laugh.
Ori will likely point to the Listed $175,000 Noble Damsel, a one-mile turf test for fillies and mares 3-years-old and up on November 27 here.
Casse indicated he will have a big presence in New York this winter for a meet that will be contested exclusively over Tapeta. His significant stock will include a number of horses with past Tapeta experience at Woodbine, whose season comes to a close on December 13.

articles.title_orig: World Wide Technology to Expand Technology Collaboration with Saint Louis University and Become Official Jersey Partner of Billiken Athletics | Newswise
articles.title_zh: World Wide Technology to Expand Technology Collaboration with Saint Louis University and Become Official Jersey Partner of Billiken Athletics | Newswise
articles.content_orig:
New Billikens Athletics Jersey with World Wide Technology Logo
World Wide Technology to Expand Technology Collaboration with Saint Louis University and Become Official Jersey Partner of Billiken Athletics
Newswise — ST. LOUIS – Saint Louis University (SLU) and World Wide Technology (WWT) announced a strategic partnership that brings together WWT’s expertise in technology, artificial intelligence and data-driven decision-making with SLU’s mission of education, research and community. Combined with a Billiken Athletics sponsorship, this expansion of SLU and WWT’s longstanding partnership will help advance priorities that benefit students, strengthen the University and contribute to the vitality of the St. Louis region.
As part of the agreement, the WWT logo will appear on all team uniforms, making WWT the first official jersey patch partner of Billiken Athletics. WWT will also serve as a strategic advisor and collaborator to accelerate the University's ability to make informed decisions through technology, data and the responsible application of AI.
“World Wide Technology’s journey from a small startup to a global technology leader demonstrates the power of investing in people, ingenuity and purpose,” said Saint Louis University President Edward Feser, Ph.D. “At SLU, we see that potential in our students every day. This partnership reflects the value of mission-driven institutions working together to cultivate talent, advance new ideas, and create opportunities for students and the communities they will serve.”
The new jersey branding will debut during Billiken Athletics games this fall. Highly visible on the court and the field, the branding signifies a deeper relationship between WWT and Billiken Athletics, and a broader collaboration across the University.
The partnership builds on a longstanding relationship between the organizations. Billiken alumni serve in roles across WWT, from technical roles to its leadership ranks, while WWT leaders have served SLU as trustees, advisors and supporters. Through internships, mentoring, philanthropy and engagement with academic and athletic programs, the two organizations have created pathways that connect learning, leadership and career opportunities.
“As an active SLU alumnus and former Billiken soccer team member, I care deeply about supporting the priorities of the University and enriching the student and fan experience,” said Jim Kavanaugh, co-founder and CEO, WWT. “This expanded partnership between SLU and WWT gives the University and its athletics department more capabilities to advance their AI and digital transformation, while growing and developing student athletes.”
WWT and SLU are exploring collaborations that upskill America’s workforce through degree programs and specialized trainings offered by the University’s colleges and Center for Workforce Development. By working together, WWT and SLU can help shape how the latest technologies are deployed to support the missions of higher education and healthcare across the globe.
“Technology decisions at a university impact students, faculty, staff and the community around them,” said Joe Koenig, WWT president SLU alumnus and former Billiken soccer team member. “Through enhanced research capabilities including data analysis, new technology development by faculty and students’ digital experiences, WWT will serve as a strategic advisor for SLU, applying our AI and data expertise to help the University make informed decisions, operate more efficiently and use AI responsibly.”
The partnership makes it possible to bring the benefits of AI to the community, engaging through digital platforms. Fans will have enhanced experiences and data insights will help inform student and athletic programs and reflect community feedback.
“Today’s collegiate athletics landscape requires institutions to think creatively and strategically about how they engage fans, support student-athletes and position their programs for long-term success,” said Chris May, director of athletics at Saint Louis University. “World Wide Technology is a trusted strategic partner whose expertise in building a best-in-class culture and organization has been central to the success of Billiken Athletics. We are thrilled to build on this relationship as we take the next step in our technology strategy and transformation, ultimately enhancing the experience for our Billiken student-athletes and fans.”
About Saint Louis University
Founded in 1818, Saint Louis University is one of the nation’s oldest and most prestigious Catholic research institutions. Rooted in Jesuit values and its pioneering history as the first university west of the Mississippi River, SLU offers more than 12,000 students a rigorous, transformative education that challenges and prepares them for lives of purpose. As a nationally recognized leader in research and innovation, SLU is an R1 research university, advancing groundbreaking, life-changing discoveries that promote the greater good.
About World Wide Technology
World Wide Technology (WWT) is a global technology solutions provider helping organizations make a new world happen by turning ambition into real-world outcomes. Founded in 1990, WWT brings together strategy, deep technical expertise and world-class technology partnerships to help public- and private-sector organizations design, build and scale intelligent AI, digital, cybersecurity, cloud and infrastructure solutions. Through its Advanced Technology Center (ATC), a collaborative ecosystem featuring state-of-the-art hardware and software, WWT enables clients and partners to conceptualize, test and validate innovative technology and then deploy solutions at scale using its global integration and distribution capabilities. With more than 14,000 team members and over 60 locations worldwide, WWT's culture — grounded in core values and leadership philosophies — has been recognized by Fortune and Great Place to Work® for its commitment to innovation, trust and creating a great place to work for all. WWT provides products and services to large enterprises, global service providers and public sector clients in up to 130 countries across six continents. Softchoice, a World Wide Technology company, supports commercial and SMB markets in the U.S. and Canada.

articles.title_orig: Trump selects Katie Zacharia as next White House press secretary
articles.title_zh: Trump selects Katie Zacharia as next White House press secretary
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump has selected Katie Zacharia, a conservative commentator who worked briefly at the Department of Homeland Security, as his new press secretary.
Zacharia thanked Trump in a social media post Friday, writing, “Serving President Trump and the American people at this critical 250-year mark is the honor of a lifetime.”
In announcing her selection earlier Friday, Trump highlighted her work for Truth Social, the Trump Media & Technology Group and her frequent appearances on Fox and Newsmax.
“She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning,” he added.
Trump in recent days called a number of his close allies and advisers, including former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt to seek their opinion of Zacharia, a person familiar with the discussions said. And the president sought Leavitt’s counsel before making a final decision and offering Zacharia the position, they said.
CNN has reached out to Zacharia, who was in the Oval Office with Trump earlier Friday morning, according to a person familiar.
Zacharia’s selection came about quickly. As of last week, she was not being considered for the role, another person familiar said.
Throughout the search to replace Leavitt, the White House struggled with higher-profile names, several of whom had previously criticized Trump. On multiple occasions, senior officials had narrowed down the list, only to find that candidates had said something negative about the president, disqualifying them from the position, according a White House official.
“The work ahead is to continue delivering strong results for our Country and communicating to the American people the major wins that this Administration is making every single day,” Zacharia wrote on X.
“I look forward to working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country, to get that record out,” she said, adding that “following the fabulous Karoline Leavitt is a high standard, and one worth meeting.”
Zacharia’s been a frequent guest on Fox, Newsmax and CNN.
“She’s a friend of most of you,” Trump told reporters while leaving the White House on Friday. “I know she likes people — she likes all of you. Actually, I don’t know if that’s good or bad, but we just hired a new press secretary, and she’s going to be, I think, terrific.”
Zacharia served as a senior communications adviser at the Trump Media and Technology Group and Truth Social since June, which followed a two-month stint as a senior official at the Department of Homeland Security — experiences that Trump also highlighted in his social media post, along with her work in his campaigns.
Zacharia, who has young children and lives in California, commuted back and forth to Washington when she was filling in at DHS. At the time, she told a friend the commute was not sustainable, according to a source familiar with the matter.
Zacharia has also served as a legal adviser for Fix California, a conservative group founded by Trump ally Richard Grenell.
She first came to Washington as an intern for the Republican National Committee during the George W. Bush administration in 2006.
This story has been updated with additional reporting.

articles.title_orig: Jackson County prepares for world’s biggest earthquake drill on Thursday
articles.title_zh: Jackson County prepares for world’s biggest earthquake drill on Thursday
articles.content_orig:
Published 11:03 am Friday, October 9, 2026
Jackson County is asking residents to prepare for the Great ShakeOut, the world’s largest earthquake drill scheduled for 10:15 a.m. Thursday, Oct. 15.
Millions of individuals across the globe will practice Drop, Cover and Hold On, the official safety procedure to protect oneself during an earthquake.
This annual event provides an opportunity for people in homes, schools and businesses to assess their disaster preparedness, improve their emergency safety plans and practice what to do in the event of a real earthquake.
For more information and resources to plan your drill, visit shakeout.org/Oregon .
Completing a few small tasks ahead of time, such as assembling a basic emergency supply kit and determining your shelter strategy, helps to assure that you and your family will know what to do and have the supplies you need to be safe wherever you are.
For more preparedness resources and tips, visit ready.gov .
Jackson County will also be conducting a test of the Jackson Alerts notification system in conjunction with the Great ShakeOut.
This service provides critical information quickly for a variety of emergency situations.
To raise awareness and educate the public on disaster preparedness, residents registered with Jackson Alerts will receive a test alert through all listed delivery methods — call, text and email — between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m.
Register, update your Jackson Alerts account and/or find more information at jacksoncountyor.gov/alerts .
