articles.title_orig: High surf floods Newport Beach as Tropical Storm Rachel-driven waves pound coast
articles.title_zh: High surf floods Newport Beach as Tropical Storm Rachel-driven waves pound coast
articles.content_orig:
A hurricane swell and an overlapping south swell, combined with high tide, flooded the streets of Newport Beach and Laguna Beach with salt water Friday morning, shutting down roadways and snarling traffic throughout the coastal towns.
City workers scrambled to pump the salt water back to the sea.
And the worst is likely yet to come. Waves are expected to get even bigger over the weekend, with tides even higher in the morning hours. Rain from Tropical Storm Rachel is also in the forecast this weekend.
The National Weather Service issued a coastal flood advisory for Orange County beaches that will remain in effect until 2 p.m. Tuesday, warning of flooding in low-lying coastal areas during high tides.
Both coastal towns have suffered severe erosion in recent months, as consistent swells have battered the coastline, eroding the beach buffer between the ocean and the roadways. Friday morning, seawater flooded nearby streets, despite city efforts to build berms, set up sandbags and hold back the ocean.
Newport Beach officials said they were declaring a local emergency Friday to get resources quickly and asked people to stay clear of the flooded areas on the Balboa Peninsula as water was drained and the aftermath of the flooding was cleaned up. Police were allowing only residents into the area.
City staffers were out Friday assessing any damage to homes, and about 40 to 50 workers had been tasked with pumping water out of the streets, city spokesperson Georgia Rios said.
Newport Beach maintains a network of 86 tidal valves designed to prevent rising ocean water from backing up through storm drains, along with 18 pumps used to remove standing water from streets near the harbor. The city has previously identified the Balboa Peninsula, Balboa Island, Newport Island and other low-lying harborfront neighborhoods as areas particularly vulnerable to flooding during unusually high tides.
Another six crews were rebuilding berms on local beaches, with more flooding anticipated through the weekend, Rios said.
Utilities Director Mark Vukojevic said an estimated 20 streets flooded Friday morning, similar to July 2020 when water from the ocean rushed into the streets during an episode of extremely high tide.
The water overtopped the beaches, flattening out the berms, then made its way to streets, he said.
Drains throughout the low-lying areas that feed out to the harbor were closed, because the tide was high. If they were opened, Vukojevic said, water would also rise up from the harbor into the streets.
“It would make the streets 10 times worse,” he said. “The water has nowhere to go, so we’re trying to pump it out. The relief comes when the tide goes down, that’s why it takes a couple hours after the tide goes down to drain out.”
A dozen more pumps have been added to the peninsula for the weekend and added crews will be on hand, he said.
Vukojevic was unsure Friday afternoon if homes flooded, but said he saw some water entering garages.
The city did not pump out any private properties, he said.
Councilmember Erik Weigand said he was stuck in bumper-to-bumper traffic on Friday afternoon while trying to get onto the peninsula to meet with Brett Sanders, director of the UC Irvine Climate Collaboration, to assess the conditions that contributed to the flooding.
“We’re in a current situation that this will keep occurring the next few days,” Weigand said. “It may just be too much Mother Nature impacting us. We’re just going to keep trying everything we can. Our guys are going to be out there constantly in the next week, doing everything in their power to assist where we can.”
While the water was receding from some of the flooded areas by mid-afternoon Friday, sections from 6th to 17th streets were still underwater, he said.
Weigand wasn’t sure if homes were impacted by flooding, or how many, though he said he saw some online videos from areas around the Wedge and the upper 50th streets that showed water flooding into yards and possibly into homes.
“I think we’re doing everything in our power to make sure we can protect property if we can,” he said. “The city is doing the best it can to protect homes and utilize heavy equipment that can build up berms.”
Weigand remembered times growing up in Newport Beach when streets would flood. And then, there was July 4, 2020, when Balboa Peninsula streets flooded and cars were pushed around in the parking lot. There was also some similar summer flooding in 2010.
“But I haven’t seen it this severe,” he said of the latest flooding. “To the extent it is happening at more than one area, throughout our entire coastline, is definitely, I think, an effect of the Kelvin wave, meets swell, meets high tide. I think, overall, we have the perfect storm.”
A Kelvin wave is a warm-water anomaly that travels from around the equator and pushes water levels higher for extended periods.
And what’s on the horizon could make matters even worse — an inch of rain is forecast late Saturday through Monday morning.
Newport Beach Bike Rentals owner Dave Shaw said business was slow Friday all morning, but traffic was moving through the peninsula by the late afternoon.
One thing they aren’t renting out – electric bikes.
He’s bracing for the weekend, unsure of what is ahead. The beaches have been busy with Arizona schools out for fall break, and tourists coming to the beach to beat the heat.
“It’s going to happen all weekend,” he said of the flooding potential. “We’ll figure it out as it comes.”
Bill Sharp, who has lived in West Newport for 65 years, said he has seen streets in the low-lying areas flood over the decades. But Friday’s scene was something different.
“I’ve never seen it like this, ever,” Sharp said. “There’s been moments where it’s coming up and washed into the streets in certain spots. But this is from River Jetties to the Wedge, it’s coming over the berms and filling the streets.”
“It’s unprecedented,” he added.
Usually, the flooding comes when high tides, surf and rain combine in winter months — the rain raising the water levels — but rarely does the ocean water flow into the streets during dry summer months. The region is even on the tail end of a heat wave.
Sharp said he walked through the shin-deep water in the roadway at 51st Street Friday morning.
“It’s flowing heavily over, water rushing from the ocean to the street,” he said. “It’s going over the berms, all the way to the houses. A series of berms and dikes are diverting it to the streets.”
While houses weren’t “falling into the ocean,” he said a number of the homes had drenched front yards and water was flowing around structures and into the streets.
“There’s not massive destruction, but everyone is getting wet,” Sharp said.
At the Wedge, where the local surfing community has been sounding the alarm for months about the recent speed of erosio n, bodysurfer Sean Starkey showed videos on social media of water gushing into the yards of multi-million-dollar beachfront homes.
Starkey said he had warned the city that a steep, natural sand berm created by the waves was hard packed enough to keep the water at bay, but city crews flattened it out to create a slope. That allowed the water to run up the small sliver of sand left, he argued.
Weigand said crews have been out at the Wedge since June trying to move sand around. He wondered if there was enough sand to work with in the first place after recent erosion to create a big enough berm along the beaches.
And, beaches that have wide swaths of sand flooded over, like near Newport Elementary, he said.
“You can only protect so much with the manpower you have,” Weigand said. “We have 7 miles of shoreline; it’s impossible to protect it all, in a situation like this where it’s affecting everything. There’s swell, high tides and Kelvin waves. It’s a trifecta of trouble.”
Sharp has seen a thousand 6-foot swells, with 6-foot tides, like what showed up on Friday, he said. But this time, it was different, he said.
“It’s a foot higher than it’s supposed to be,”

articles.title_orig: Real-world data link fezolinetant to fewer nighttime awakenings
articles.title_zh: Real-world data link fezolinetant to fewer nighttime awakenings
articles.content_orig:
Fezolinetant (Veozah) was linked to objective and patient-reported sleep gains in OPTION-VMS, with no new safety signals observed.
Fezolinetant (Veozah) was associated with statistically significant improvements in objective and patient-reported sleep measures among women with bothersome vasomotor symptoms (VMS) in a second preliminary analysis of the ongoing OPTION-VMS study, according to Marla Shapiro, CM, MDCM, CCFP, MHSc, FRCPC, FCFP, MSCP. 1
The prospective, multicenter US study, which was presented at the International Menopause Society 20th World Congress on Menopause, enrolled women aged 40 to 75 years. As of March 2026, 993 users of nonhormonal therapy were enrolled, 859 of whom completed baseline and at least 1 postbaseline assessment. Treatments were grouped by initial prescription: fezolinetant, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs/SNRIs), and other nonhormonal therapies. Sleep was assessed objectively with a medical-grade wearable actigraphy device and subjectively with the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Sleep Disturbance Short Form 8b at weeks 4, 8, and 12. 1 An earlier preliminary analysis had also reported sleep improvements with fezolinetant. 2
At week 12, fezolinetant was associated with reductions in wakefulness after sleep onset (least squares mean change, −9.45 minutes; 95% CI, −13.93 to −4.96), sleep latency (−1.24 minutes; 95% CI, −1.81 to −0.67), and nighttime awakenings (−2.61; 95% CI, −4.07 to −1.15), as well as increased sleep efficiency (+1.95%; 95% CI, 0.93-2.97) and improved PROMIS total T-scores (−5.69; 95% CI, −6.95 to −4.44) (all P < .001). Improvements were also significant at weeks 4 and 8. 1
Apart from a low-dose SSRI approved in the United States, nonhormonal VMS treatments had historically been used off label, Shapiro noted. The other nonhormonal group consisted primarily of gabapentin, with some pregabalin and clonidine. Results were limited to within-group changes from baseline.
"The study was not designed to compare treatment groups. So they're not head-to-head comparisons," Shapiro said.
SSRIs/SNRIs were not associated with statistically significant improvements in any actigraphy end point. In the other nonhormonal group, the only significant actigraphy improvement was in wakefulness after sleep onset, at weeks 4 and 12. Patient-reported sleep improved significantly in both groups, with PROMIS scores moving from the mild to the no-disturbance range by week 4 with SSRIs/SNRIs and by week 8 with other nonhormonal therapies. 1
No new safety signals emerged. The incidence of drug-related treatment-emergent adverse events, including those leading to drug withdrawal or interruption, was very low with fezolinetant, and no drug-related serious adverse events or hepatotoxicity occurred. 1
"There were 2 cumulative cases of non-serious mild elevated LFTs, neither of which led to treatment or study discontinuation," Shapiro said. Headache and upper respiratory infection were the most commonly reported events, each at a rate of approximately 1.5%.
Findings were consistent across racially and ethnically diverse women, women older than 65 years, women in the menopause transition, and women with obesity. Together with SKYLIGHT trial data from nearly 3000 women and postapproval experience, the findings reinforced a favorable benefit-risk profile for fezolinetant. 3

articles.title_orig: Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar Review: A Great Home Theater Option All By Itself
articles.title_zh: Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar Review: A Great Home Theater Option All By Itself
articles.content_orig:
You won’t feel the need to immediately add a subwoofer to this one.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
When Bose proclaimed that the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar was its "loudest, deepest and most immersive" model yet, I still assumed it would need a subwoofer." Yet when I first connected the company's latest soundbar to my TV, I quickly realized it didn't need the extra bass boost. The combination of CleanBass tech and QuietPort acoustics provide enough low-end tone that you aren't likely to crave an additional, pricey sub. Since the soundbar alone is already $1,099 , that was a welcome surprise.
I get it: There's not a ton of room for innovation when it comes to the design of soundbars. They all have to be elongated and rectangular to be able to contain a collection of drivers without blocking your TV. But there is room for improvement when it comes to the general look of soundbars, and that's where Bose stepped up its game on the Lifestyle Ultra.
The speaker is short and wide, just like you'd expect, but the textured, knit-fabric grille elevates the overall aesthetic. This is more apparent on the white colorway than the black, and luckily the lighter color is exactly what was sent to me for review. Bose also opted for a glass top where the competition typically uses a plastic panel or just buttons. The glass portion doesn't extend all the way to the edges though, so there's room for the up-firing drivers to do their thing.
Another excellent design choice was the volume controls. Bose installed a touch-enabled, circular panel that allows you to spin your finger clockwise and counterclockwise to raise and lower the volume. You can also just tap the "+" or "-" if you'd rather. There's an area in the middle of the circle that you can tap to play, pause or skip tracks, as well as touch-based controls for Bluetooth, disabling the soundbar's microphone and summoning Alexa. All of that is positioned on the right side of the glass panel.
Inside, Bose arranged a collection of nine drivers for the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar's acoustic architecture. There are six full-range drivers, two of which are up-firing and the other four are front facing. Additionally, a center-mounted tweeter assists with dialogue clarity, while two so-called PhaseGuide drivers spread sound horizontally. To calibrate all of that for your living room, Bose's CustomTune feature uses the microphone in your Android or iOS device to analyze the space (speaker layout, surfaces and seating) and optimize the soundbar's output.
Like most soundbars these days, the Lifestyle Ultra only has a single HDMI eARC input. This isn't a problem per se, but if you need HDMI 2.0 passthrough for things like game consoles, just note that it's not available here.
The Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar is very much a plug-and-play device. Once you connect it to power and your TV, it's ready to go. However, you'll want to download the Bose app and run the CustomTune audio calibration ASAP to tailor the soundbar's output to the acoustics of your living room or home theater space. Of course, if you add either the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer or Lifestyle Ultra Speakers to the soundbar, you'll need to repeat the CustomTune process.
Once all of that is complete, the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar provides a solid boost to your TV audio. The up-firing and PhaseGuide drivers offer a pleasant level of immersion and dimensional audio, which is apparent on shows like Drive to Survive and Masters of the Air. The bass output is the most impressive thing about this soundbar, though. It's enough that users in small to medium spaces likely won't immediately feel the need to add a subwoofer. Even after several weeks of testing, I'm still baffled by the low-end performance when a sound effect demands that portion of the frequency range.
This bass is abundantly apparent for music, too. Sylvan Esso's "Flood Season" has ample lows for the bass guitar riffs and kick drum, while more bass-heavy tracks, like Russian Circles' "Empath," maintain the tonal depth without getting muddy. I also appreciate how the center tweeter allows vocals to consistently float on top of the mix. This makes albums like Hayley Williams' Ego Death At A Bachelorette Party particularly enjoyable.
As I already mentioned, Bose allows you to expand your home theater system with the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer and Lifestyle Ultra Speakers. Unless you have a larger space, or just crave the extra immersion that rear speakers can provide when watching movies or TV shows, I don't think either are absolutely necessary here.
The speakers are $349 each and the sub comes in at $899, but if you opt for the Home Theater Set or Surround Sound Set (Lifestyle Ultra bundles), you can save a few hundred dollars. (Oddly, Bose doesn't offer savings on the Extra Bass Set, which is the soundbar and subwoofer).
I tested the add-ons one at a time. First, I added the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer to the soundbar — perhaps the most likely additional purchase for most people. This achieves the obvious result of adding more bass, which could be preferential if you plan for the Lifestyle Ultra gear to pull double duty as your main music setup. But even in my living room, which is open to the main dining area and kitchen, the soundbar alone was still adequate for music.
I then added two Lifestyle Ultra Speakers as rear units, which I quickly discovered would be my preferred way to bolster the soundbar's performance. Since the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar holds its own in the bass department, its only true deficiency is directional audio and overall immersion. Add those two speakers to the rear and that weakness is fixed, and disabling the subwoofer doesn't result in much sacrifice to overall output. I only really noticed a big difference in certain scenes with really booming effects, like certain parts of the first episode of Masters of the Air (no spoilers from me) .
AirPlay, Google Cast and Spotify Connect are all available on the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar for quick and easy music streaming. You can also opt for Bluetooth, if you prefer, but I find the three methods I mentioned are more convenient for getting audio from a phone or laptop to a soundbar.
The Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar does well enough on its own that Bose's primary competition is other companies that claim they've built all-in-one TV speakers that don't need a separate subwoofer. My top pick in that category is Samsung's QS90H , which costs $99 less at full price. This 7.1.2-channel soundbar not only provides adequate bass without a sub, but it has Samsung's Convertible Fit tech that allows you to place it flat or mounted upright. Sensors in the soundbar then reconfigure the output based on how it's sitting. Samsung included lots of other features, but some of them, like Q-Symphony, require a recent Samsung TV to use.
Another excellent option for a true all-in-one soundbar is the Sonos Arc Ultra . The company's flagship model is equipped with Sound Motion technology that handles the bass in a 9.1.4-channel setup. That last number indicates two additional height channels compared to the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar and the QS90H. The Arc Ultra not only has more channels overall, but it also contains more drivers than either the Bose or Samsung options, with 14 of those total. At full price, the Arc Ultra costs the same as the Lifestyle Ultra, but Sonos currently has it on sale for $899 .
Editor's note: Bose is offering a $200 discount on the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar through October 11.
Perhaps Bose's hesitance to label the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar as an all-in-one unit comes down to sales. I'm sure the company would prefer for you to buy the pricey subwoofer for a speaker combo that's common to living rooms. I'd recommend spending extra money on a pair of Lifestyle Ultra Speakers instead, and configure your home theater for better immersion rather than overly booming bass.
No matter what you choose, it won't change the fact that the Lifes

articles.title_orig: From H-1B to CEO: How Satya Nadella traveled the path the U.S. just cut off for Microsoft workers
articles.title_zh: From H-1B to CEO: How Satya Nadella traveled the path the U.S. just cut off for Microsoft workers
articles.content_orig:
India called comments by U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance about immigrants from the country "deeply offensive" in an official government statement published on Friday.
Vance said on Thursday that the Trump administration wants foreign and local companies to "employ American workers," and that they "cannot lay off American workers and then replace them with foreign indentured servants."
He was speaking as the U.S. Department of Labor announced it would suspend Microsoft , Adobe and several major Indian information technology companies from its Permanent Labor Certification program, meaning they cannot apply for permanent residency for their employees on H-1 B visas.
Around 70% of H-1B beneficiaries in 2025 were born in India , per official data .
In a statement on Friday, India's Ministry of External Affairs accused Vance of using " terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations."
"Such descriptions are unwarranted and ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem," the statement said.
Vance's office did not immediately respond to a comment request from CNBC.
Vance was critical of Microsoft, accusing the company of replacing 6,000 laid-off workers with people on H-1B visas.
The Indian foreign ministry assured its citizens that measures announced by the U.S. will not affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents.
"Talent mobility adds value to both economies," the statement said, adding that the suspensions "do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries."
The Indian companies affected by the ban include Cognizant , Infosys , Capgemini, Tata Consultancy Services , Wipro and HCL .
NASSCOM, the IT industry body, said in a statement that Indian technology companies have "significantly reduced their dependence on H-1B visas" over the last few years, and are expanding domestic hiring to their U.S. workforces.
The largest Indian IT company, Tata Consultancy Services, said its H-1B applications were in "single digits" in the last two years, and it intends to hire another 15,000 people in the U.S. over the next five years.
In June, a federal judge blocked the $100,000 H-1B visa fee U.S. President Donald Trump imposed last year.

articles.title_zh: Must-Win MAGA Candidate Exposed Blaming Wife in Fraud Probe
articles.content_orig:
A leaked deposition shows Senate candidate Ken Paxton defended himself against fraud allegations by claiming he doesnât remember and blaming his now-estranged wife.
The Texas attorney generalâs never-before-seen 2014 testimony from a fraud probe was given to The New York Times by someone who opposes his election and was then independently verified by The Times.
It was the latest leak to hit the struggling MAGA candidate in the must-win race, as he has also faced a slow drip of audio leaks.
The deposition was part of a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) investigation into a technology start-up in McKinney, Texas, called Servergy Inc.
Senate candidate Ken Paxton, pictured campaigning with President Trump on October 7, has been hit with another leak, this time a 2014 deposition in a fraud probe.
The SEC grilled Paxton, who represented the state district where it was based, on whether he hid that the company compensated him for recruiting investors, the Times reported, as its founder, Bill Mapp, was accused of making false statements to investors.
Paxton has long fought allegations of corruption and questions about his ballooning wealth for years while serving in public office, but he has never been convicted.
By clicking â SUBSCRIBE â you agree to our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy .
Speaking under oath to federal lawyers in 2014, Paxton defended himself while using phrases such as âI donât rememberâ and âI donât recallâ more than 200 times, according to the report.
He passed the buck to his now-estranged wife, Angela Paxton, when asked about his tax returns, which appeared to contradict part of his testimony.
âI havenât prepared a tax return in a long time because I donât have time, so typically, actually my wife actually does them,â Paxton said.
Ken and Angela Paxton in 2021. She filed for divorce last year.
Lawyers questioned Paxton about emails in which the start-upâs founder, Mapp, appeared to offer him a commission for recruiting investors.
Paxton claimed he did not remember reading many of Mappâs emails, according to the report, and did not perform services for the company.
When confronted with his own tax returns, showing Paxton had disclosed $100,000 for âlegal servicesâ to the company, he pointed the finger at his then-wife.
Paxton met with Mapp at a Dairy Queen to give him a check for his investment with Servergy, but Mapp rejected the money and instead gifted him 100,000 shares of stock, the report said.
âHe said, I canât take your money. God doesnât want me to take your money,ââ Paxton told lawyers in the deposition.
When asked why Mapp would give him shares for free, Paxton said in the deposition, âIt was not logical,â and claimed, âBill is a spiritual person.â He also said he did not ask a lawyer if it were appropriate to accept the shares.
He also told the lawyers he could not remember where the certificate proving he owned the stocks was.
Paxton listed the shares as stocks on his annual financial reports filed with state ethics regulators, but a Texas ethics law expert told The Times that Paxton may have violated state rules by not disclosing the shares as a gift.
During the deposition, Paxton also said he had more than $400,000 invested in various companies, but he said he did not have time to track his investments.
The federal judge dismissed the SECâs fraud case against Paxton in 2017, saying he had no obligation to tell investors he had received something of value from the company.
Last year, Angela Paxton filed for divorce, accusing her husband of infidelity. The Daily Beast asked her for comment on the report but did not immediately hear back. She declined to comment to The Times.
The Daily Beast also asked for comment from Paxtonâs campaign. In response to The Times, a Paxton adviser called the leaked deposition a distraction and argued the candidate âhas been politically persecuted for years for standing up to the establishment, and Texans have seen through it every time.â

articles.title_orig: Intel Is Reportedly Launching New CPUs On Old Sockets That Support DDR4 Memory
articles.title_zh: Intel Is Reportedly Launching New CPUs On Old Sockets That Support DDR4 Memory
articles.content_orig:
This is, of course, due to the AI-fueled RAMpocalypse.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
Intel is reportedly releasing new CPUs built on LGA 1700 sockets, according to motherboard manufacturer Gigabyte . The LGA 1700 has been around since 2021, which is a really long time in processor land. Why use relatively ancient technology in brand-new processors that are set to release next year? It all comes down to the price of memory, according to a report by PC Gamer .
LGA 1700 sockets offer support for both DDR5 and DDR4 memory, so the running theory is that upcoming refreshes of Raptor Lake and Alder Lake processors will be configurable to use DDR4 RAM. This is likely to accommodate the ongoing AI-fueled RAMpocalypse , in which memory prices have skyrocketed. Simply put, DDR4 RAM is a lot cheaper than DDR5. Folks can pick up a 32GB DDR4 kit for around $210 , but a 32GB DDR5 kit costs upwards of $480 .
Intel hasn't confirmed this theory, but VP Robert Hallock recently said that Raptor Lake chips would be sticking around for "years to come." He also suggested that DDR4 integration is one of the primary reasons. "LGA 1700 is still a good socket. Lots of people are still interested in DDR4, so we'll keep offering," he said.
This isn't that surprising, given that many of the company's current line of processors can already be configured to use DDR4 memory. DDR4 isn't as fast as DDR5, but the older memory type is still fine for the vast majority of modern PC games . Testing has revealed that DDR5 sticks deliver a 1 to ten percent FPS improvement. However, this largely depends on the resolution the player chooses and the GPU.

articles.title_orig: Tropical Storm Rachel approaches Southern California. Here’s how much rain to expect
articles.title_zh: Tropical Storm Rachel approaches Southern California. Here’s how much rain to expect
articles.content_orig:
A hurricane swell and an overlapping south swell, combined with high tide, flooded the streets of Newport Beach and Laguna Beach with salt water Friday morning, shutting down roadways and snarling traffic throughout the coastal towns.
City workers scrambled to pump the salt water back to the sea.
And the worst is likely yet to come. Waves are expected to get even bigger over the weekend, with tides even higher in the morning hours. Rain from Tropical Storm Rachel is in the forecast this weekend.
The National Weather Service issued a coastal flood advisory for Orange County beaches that will remain in effect until 2 p.m. Tuesday, warning of flooding in low-lying coastal areas during high tides.
Both coastal towns have suffered severe erosion in recent months, as consistent swells have battered the coastline, eroding the beach buffer between the ocean and the roadways. Friday morning, seawater flooded nearby streets, despite city efforts to build berms, set up sandbags and hold back the ocean.
Newport Beach was preparing in the morning to declare a local emergency to get resources quickly and officials are asking people to stay clear of the flooded areas of the Balboa Peninsula, with police allowing only residents into the area. City spokesperson Georgia Rios also said cars low to the ground and Teslas should avoid the area; the electric cars can catch fire in salt water.
City staffers are out assessing any damage to homes, and about 40 to 50 workers are involved in pumping water out of the streets, Rios said.
Newport Beach maintains a network of 86 tidal valves designed to prevent rising ocean water from backing up through storm drains, along with 18 pumps used to remove standing water from streets near the harbor. The city has previously identified the Balboa Peninsula, Balboa Island, Newport Island and other low-lying harborfront neighborhoods as areas particularly vulnerable to flooding during unusually high tides.
Another six crews are rebuilding berms on the beach, with more flooding anticipated through the weekend, Rios said.
Bill Sharp, who has lived in West Newport for 65 years, said he has seen streets in the low-lying areas flood over the decades. But Friday’s scene was something different.
“I’ve never seen it like this, ever,” Sharp said. “There’s been moments where it’s coming up and washed into the streets in certain spots. But this is from River Jetties to the Wedge, it’s coming over the berms and filling the streets.”
“It’s unprecedented,” he added.
Usually, the flooding comes when high tides, surf and rain combine in winter months, but rarely in dry summer months.
Sharp said he walked through the shin-deep water in the roadway at 51st Street.
“It’s flowing heavily over, water rushing from the ocean to the street,” he said. “It’s going over the berms, all the way to the houses. A series of berms and dikes are diverting it to the streets.”
While houses weren’t “falling into the ocean,” he said a number of the homes had drenched front yards and water was flowing around structures and into the streets.
“There’s not massive destruction, but everyone is getting wet,” Sharp said.
At the Wedge, where the local surfing community has been sounding the alarm for months about the recent speed of erosio n, bodysurfer Sean Starkey showed videos on social media of water gushing into the yards of multi-million-dollar beachfront homes.
“Starkey had gone out the night before to check on the beach as water was getting near the homes. He had warned the city that a natural sand berm created by the waves was hard packed enough to keep the water at bay, but city crews flattened it out to create a slope, which allowed the water to run up the small sliver of what’s left of the sand, he said.
Sharp has seen a thousand 6-foot swells, with 6-foot tides, like what showed up on Friday. But this time, it was different, he said.
“It’s a foot higher than it’s supposed to be,” he said. “Whether it’s the Kelvin wave, or the water is thicker, or whatever it is, the waves are coming in with an extra foot of water underneath them.”
A Kelvin wave is a warm-water anomaly that travels from around the equator and pushes water levels higher for extended periods.
Sandbags are available at Newport Beach’s Corporate Yard, 592 Superior Ave. For those on the peninsula, lifeguards have stocked up in the back of their trucks to get them to residents, Rios said.
“We are going to have staff out all weekend, we are expecting a continued amount of flooding, especially on Sunday and Monday. We have all staff out right now, monitoring utilities, pumps, reinforcing and adding more berms and have public safety out here to help,” she added.
Newport Beach Lifeguard Chief Brian O’Rourke said it’s an “all-hands” event.
“We’ll be definitely monitoring it and responding as necessary,” he said. “We’re definitely concerned from beach erosion to flooding, and potential property concerns. We’re keeping tabs on everything and responding as necessary in the most efficient way we can.”
The beach erosion has become so severe, he said, that even smaller-sized swells can have an impact right now.
“The waves are big, but not exceptionally huge,” he said. “So there’s some unknown force associated with this swell.”
Mike Halphide, retired Newport Beach marine safety chief, said when he went to church Friday morning at 15th Street and Balboa Boulevard, he noticed a little trickle of water in the streets. By 7:55 a.m., the boulevard was flooded to the median, an hour before the high tide peaked at 9 a.m., he said.
“Surf looks like an expression of the predicted Kelvin Wave,” he noted.
He left his car in the parking lot and walked home, he said, returning a few hours later. He watched as cars stalled out trying to get through the flood, he said, and police limited traffic access to some of the impacted streets.
The flood comes just ahead of a City Council study session set for 4 p.m. Tuesday, Oct. 13, at Newport Beach City Hall, to review the history of sand nourishment and shoreline structures, current conditions along the city’s coastline, and proposed plans and ongoing efforts to replenish sand in selected shoreline areas.

articles.title_orig: Home on verge of collapse as high tide hits Long Beach Peninsula
articles.title_zh: Home on verge of collapse as high tide hits Long Beach Peninsula
articles.content_orig:
Learn more about what storm season means for Long Beach and how you can be prepared at LBPost.com/elnino . Support useful, community-centered reporting like this with a donation .
City inspectors have declared several buildings on the Peninsula unsafe to enter after Hurricane Rachel’s high surf and tides chewed away at the shoreline, tearing apart a section of a wooden wall that is the neighborhood’s last line of defense against the ocean.
Officials issued a notice Thursday night that a large section of the bulkhead, left exposed after waves from Hurricane Marie ripped away its surrounding sand , was badly damaged over the past day and left a gap that allowed water to reach homes and side streets.
Residents stood in shin-deep flooding on Friday, with vehicle access closed at 62nd Place. Waves continued to chew at homes’ foundations along the shoreline and tear planks from the boardwalk. At least one home in the 6500 block of Seaside Walk appeared close to collapse.
Laath Martin, a city spokesperson, said inspectors are still assessing the extent of the bulkhead and boardwalk damage.
Crews rushed to make emergency repairs, pump water off the streets and fill in the exposed section with roughly 1,000 sandbags. The city is bracing for rain this weekend, and more high tides and surf are expected.
Read more: Why one small stretch of Long Beach keeps getting pounded with damaging waves
Inspectors surveyed homes threatened by water damage and red-tagged two buildings containing three units in the 6400 and 6500 blocks of Seaside Walk. The red tag means they’re too dangerous to enter.
Craig Nakano, a spokesperson for the city’s Community Development Department, said Friday that nobody has been displaced by the tagging. One property was under construction, he said, while the other was confirmed by the owner to be vacant.
A third building received a yellow tag, which means its owner may go in briefly to collect belongings but may not stay. Nakano confirmed that the owner had already found somewhere else to stay.
Two buildings were already yellow-tagged after damage from Hurricane Marie weeks ago. The latest damage brings the total to five damaged Peninsula structures, two red-tagged and three yellow-tagged. The tags are preliminary, and a red tag can be downgraded to yellow once repairs are made and inspectors sign off. Inspectors will keep checking homes twice a day.
The latest bout of strong waves — whipped up by Hurricane Rachel — came just weeks after other hurricane-charged swells battered the Long Beach coast and the Peninsula .
The city is planning a multimillion-dollar dredging project to rebuild the stretch of Peninsula beach that’s been eroded. Long-term fixes are expected to be even more expensive.
In the meantime, storms keep rolling in.
Bryan Lewis, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, said high surf and tide are expected to rise precipitously each day through Sunday, with tides reaching 7.5 feet high on Saturday and nearly 8 feet high on Sunday morning around 10 a.m. Waves are currently ranging from 4 to 7  feet high, but are expected to rise to up to 8 feet by Sunday, he said.
Conditions on Sunday evening and Monday morning, he said, will mirror Saturday, and likely will not relent in strength until Wednesday morning.
The NWS expects to announce a flood warning later Friday. They currently have an advisory running through Tuesday. Warnings are usually triggered when coastal buoys the Service monitors — in this case ones in the San Pedro Channel and city harbor — are routinely hit with high enough surf, Lewis explained.
This storm could also bring rain and wind. The city expects up to a half-inch of precipitation this weekend and gusts strong enough to knock down trees and power lines.
“Protecting our residents is our top priority as high surf and erosion impact our Peninsula community,” Mayor Rex Richardson said in a statement. He praised emergency crews and urged residents to “be prepared and follow City guidance.”
Lewis said rain showers could start in the area as early as Friday night and Saturday morning, with a second storm system hitting the area on Monday. Showers are expected to total between a half inch and three quarters of an inch of rain.
“This will bring additional rain, so that’s kind of separate from what tropical storm Rachel could be responsible for,” Lewis said.

articles.title_orig: Trump establishes committee to investigate Federal Reserve's Lisa Cook in latest effort to fire her
articles.title_zh: Trump establishes committee to investigate Federal Reserve's Lisa Cook in latest effort to fire her
articles.content_orig:
BREAKING: Trump eases Russia sanctions to allow Putin to release diesel fuel onto the global market amid price spike
President Donald Trump on Friday signed an order directing the attorney general and other top federal officials to establish a committee to investigate Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook, in his latest attempt to fire her.
“By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, I hereby establish a committee of inquiry (Committee) to investigate allegations that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa D. Cook made false statements in connection with one or more mortgage instruments,” read a presidential memorandum posted to the White House website.
It said that the committee would “investigate the allegations against Governor Cook and report to me whether there is ‘cause’ for Governor Cook’s removal.”
“Governor Cook may submit a written position statement to the Committee regarding the allegations,” the memorandum said.
The unprecedented White House announcement comes after a top White House official in August wrote a letter to Cook , saying that Trump was considering removing her from the Federal Reserve board.
The White House memorandum said that Cook “shall appear at the hearing and be examined by the Committee,” as well as “present argument, written evidence, and written witness statements regarding the evidence and allegations.”
The committee is set to meet Nov. 5 for the hearing, two days after the midterm elections. No president has ever fired a top Fed official.
“In light of the President’s repeated statements that he has already decided to fire Governor Cook — regardless of the facts and evidence —  we have grave doubts that this ‘hearing’ is a legitimate one that would conform to the law,” said Abbe Lowell and Norm Eisen, Cook’s attorneys.
“But if it is anything close to objective, the conclusion will be that Governor Cook did not commit mortgage fraud, leaving no cause to remove her from the Federal Reserve Board.”
Lowell and Eisen said they have engaged with the White House to determine if this is a “genuine” process and that Cook “welcomes the opportunity to present the facts so she can clear her name and demonstrate there is no legal basis to fire her.”
The memo follows a Supreme Court ruling in June, which allowed Cook to remain in her job for now. But the justices did not permanently block Trump from removing Cook, instead ruling that she had the right to an opportunity to defend herself.
Trump’s latest move stems from allegations first leveled against Cook in August 2025 by Federal Housing Finance Agency chief Bill Pulte. Trump amplified those allegations on social media and, citing a “criminal referral” he said Pulte had sent to the Justice Department, attempted to remove her from the Fed’s board.
Pulte alleged that Cook committed mortgage fraud, however documents obtained and reviewed by NBC News later revealed that Cook declared that the property in question was to be used as a “vacation home” and not her primary residence.
The Federal Reserve declined to comment on Friday’s developments.
Other top Trump administration officials, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, reportedly have similar mortgage situations.
Former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin have all called more than one property their “primary residence” on mortgage applications, according to a report last year from ProPublica .
Cook, a governor on the Federal Reserve’s board, has a permanent vote on interest rates. Trump and Pulte’s attacks on Cook came amid a long-running pressure campaign by the administration to get the U.S. central bank to cut interest rates.
“President Trump is convening an illegitimate show trial in his dangerous quest to illegally take over our nation’s central bank,” said Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, which oversees the Fed.
“Instead of playing judge in a kangaroo court of his own making, Trump should end the war in Iran and cancel his chaotic tariffs,” Warren said.
Trump also recently resumed his attacks on another Fed governor, Jerome Powell. Trump claimed Sept. 30 that the former chairman was complicit in cost overruns for a construction project at the central bank’s headquarters. However, an inspector general’s report found no wrongdoing.
Trump responded to the report by writing on social media, “He should be forced to resign, IMMEDIATELY! If he doesn’t resign, he should be sued, at the highest level, by the United States Government, for either corruption or incompetence.”
Following the post, Attorney General Todd Blanche told Bloomberg News , “We’re not reopening a criminal investigation into him.”
Powell has remained on the Fed’s board despite the end of his term as chair, breaking with tradition. As long as Powell remains on the board, the Trump administration is denied the opportunity to name a new board member of the president’s choice.
Cook has consistently maintained that she did nothing wrong.
Just weeks ago, Cook’s lawyer told the White House for a second time that, “There is no legal basis for President Trump to remove Governor Cook for cause.”
“An inadvertent error is not fraud, as the President and a third of his cabinet should know because they reportedly did the same thing,” Abbe Lowell said Aug. 26. “These attacks on Governor Cook are not about real estate paperwork; they are an attempt by President Trump to force the Federal Reserve to bend to his will.”
Lowell said he and Cook were prepared to continue to fight “any illegal attempt to remove Governor Cook.”
Steve Kopack is a senior reporter at NBC News covering business and the economy.

articles.title_orig: US surpasses 4,000 measles cases with infections confirmed in 45 states: CDC - ABC News
articles.title_zh: US surpasses 4,000 measles cases with infections confirmed in 45 states: CDC - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
Most cases are among those unvaccinated or with unknown status, CDC data shows.
Measles cases in the United States have surpassed 4,000 this year, according to data updated Friday from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
A total of 4,080 cases have been confirmed, with most reported by 45 states and Washington, D.C. Eighteen of this year's total have been among international visitors to the U.S., according to the CDC.
Five measles-associated deaths have been confirmed so far in 2026, all of them in Pennsylvania, according to health officials in the state .
The CDC has only recognized two deaths so far this year, with the agency saying that "number is subject to change."
The majority of measles cases in 2026 have been confirmed among children and teenagers aged 19 and younger, according to the CDC. About one in 10 children under age 5 have been hospitalized, CDC data shows.
About 95% of cases are among people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown, according to agency data.
Meanwhile, 2% of cases are among those who have received just one dose of the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine and 2% of cases are among those who received the recommended two doses, according to the CDC.
"It's very telling," Dr. Peter Chin-Hong, an infectious diseases specialist and associate dean for regional campuses at the University of California, San Francisco, told ABC News of the breakdown in cases by vaccination status. "It's not a surprise, but it's chilling in many ways."
According to Chin-Hong, the official total of confirmed cases likely does not reflect the full picture of measles in the U.S. He said it's probable that there are many families with measles cases who never got tested.
"The story's not been fully told yet," he said. "In other words, the official numbers are only part of the picture and the reason why I think so is because the number of deaths and hospitalizations suggests that there are many more people who are infected but unaccounted."
The CDC currently recommends that people receive two doses of the MMR vaccine, the first at ages 12 to 15 months and the second between 4 and 6 years old. One dose is 93% effective, and two doses are 97% effective against measles, the CDC says.
However, CDC data shows vaccination rates have been lagging in recent years. During the 2025-26 school year, 92.4% of kindergartners received the MMR vaccine, according to data. This is lower than the 95.2% seen in the 2019-20 school year, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.
"Unlike many of the healthcare issues or diseases that affect so much of the population ... we have the tool," John Brownstein, an epidemiologist and chief innovation officer at Boston Children's Hospital and an ABC News contributor, said. "It's a vaccine that is incredibly effective and the goal is to close vaccination gaps."
He noted that authorities have a responsibility to offer straightforward advice to the public.
"We need federal leadership that is really clear on the need for vaccination. We need local communities that are providing clear guidance and education and support to make decisions," Brownstein said. "I think we need to have a very aligned view on ... the impact of measles when communities are under-vaccinated."
Some public health specialists previously told ABC News they believe the U.S. is on track to lose the elimination status it earned in 2000 .
The specialists said there are several reasons for the U.S. breaking measles case records for the second year in a row, including declining vaccination rates, people not fearing the measles virus, a loss of trust in public health institutions and a perceived lack of clear guidance and communication from the nation's top public health officials.
"I think there's a very strong chance that we would lose our elimination status because we're seeing the signs that measles is becoming continuously established here in the U.S." Brownstein said. "For a country with resources and an ability to provide protection, it's really unfortunate that we're seeing these tides turn on this very preventable disease."

articles.title_orig: Ex-German Chancellor Schröder attends Putin's birthday bash
articles.title_zh: Ex-German Chancellor Schröder attends Putin's birthday bash
articles.content_orig:
Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder attended Russian President Vladimir Putin 's birthday party, the Kremlin said Thursday.
Putin celebrated his 74th birthday in Moscow on Wednesday. The Kremlin said Putin learned that Schröder was on a business trip in the Russian capital via Russian media reports.
"The president invited his old friend to his home," the Kremlin said, with the Russian government releasing pictures of Schröder and Putin smiling and clasping hands.
Schröder , who is 82 years old, was in Moscow visiting one of the branches of the new Hyperglobus supermarket chain. The ex-German chancellor was named to the chain's supervisory board last week.
Hyperglobus was originally part of German retail company Globus Holding, which operates the Globus supermarkets in Germany and the Czech Republic.
Globus Holding also had supermarkets in Russia, but divested its stake last year, with those stores thus being spun off into separate company Hyperglobus.
Schröder, a member of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) , served as Germany's chancellor from 1998 to 2005.
Since leaving the chancellery, Schröder has worked for Russian state-owned energy firms and has also maintained personal contact with Putin.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Schröder's fondness for Russia has drawn controversy, particularly since the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Schröder's tax-payer financed Berlin office was closed in 2022 over his involvement in the Russian energy sector, and he has also faced calls by fellow party members to be expelled from the SPD.
Schröder, however, has survived the attempt to be kicked out of his party.

articles.title_orig: Europe’s Car Lobby Says EU-China Deal Can Ease Chinese Hybrid Surge ‘in Orderly Way’
articles.title_zh: Europe’s Car Lobby Says EU-China Deal Can Ease Chinese Hybrid Surge ‘in Orderly Way’
articles.content_orig:
Brussels says Beijing’s shipments could fall by more than half over four years, cutting millions of vehicles amid fears for European jobs
The EU said it has reached a landmark deal with China to “halve” its sales of hybrid cars in the bloc amid fears surging sales could kill off parts of the European car industry.
Trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič said the deal was the first of its kind and the result of “intense” negotiations with China since June to curb a trade deficit of €1.18bn (£1bn) a day, which has caused mounting tensions between the two economic powers.
The deal “opens the prospect of cutting China’s export [of hybrids] by more than a half”, Šefčovič said, adding that this would translate into a reduction in exports of plug-in and battery-powered hybrid cars by “several millions” over the next four years, said Šefčovič said Šefčovič at a press conference in Beijing on Friday.
“It is the first time that China has accepted to moderate its exports without going through the phase of prior trade tension,” he said, a reference to the usual investigations that must take place before safeguards under WTO trading rules are put in place.
China has been flooding Europe with cars , including hybrids and pure battery electric vehicles (BEVs), threatening European manufacturers. Hybrids combine an internal combustion engine with a small battery. They are sold by carmakers as a transitional step towards BEVs.
Šefčovič said the Chinese had recognised the political pressure building in every member state in Europe with “literally thousands of job losses” at risk because of the flood of cheap imports from China across many sectors including chemicals and textiles.
He said EU leaders were “clearly expecting very fast action” from the European Commission and the Chinese recognised that.
“I am glad to say that the Chinese partners appreciated this very strong political argument, and therefore, we can proceed through the negotiated solution,” he said.
“This ‌is far from the end. It’s a crucial first step, but only a first step,” Šefčovič told ‌reporters in Beijing where he had travelled to hold ​talks with his Chinese counterpart.
Earlier this week senior EU officials said they were heading to Beijing to seek what they called a “proof of concept” or pilot scheme with one sector which they hoped could then be expanded to other areas under pressure from Chinese competition.
Šefčovič said he put “so much emphasis” on the negotiations because it was “very difficult to stop” a trade war once it was declared.
As part of a 16-point agreement, Beijing and Brussels will continue negotiating on cars, export restrictions on rare earths and access to China for more food and drink from the EU.
after newsletter promotion
China said both sides would adhere to “procedures concerning company price undertakings” for hybrid cars suggesting one method of curbing sales would be to set higher minimum price tags for Chinese cars sold in Europe.
The EU commissioner will brief EU diplomats in Brussels on Sunday ahead of a leaders’ summit on Thursday.
A statement from the Chinese ministry of commerce said China is “willing … to continue facilitating the approval of export licenses for rare earths and permanent magnets destined for the EU”.
It added that both sides had “reaffirmed their commitment … to properly handle differences within the framework of WTO rules, and to continuing to stabilise and balance bilateral trade and economic relations”.
While China and the EU acknowledged “differences” between them it appears that China has accepted the EU’s request to create a new model for trade balances starting with a pilot on hybrid cars.

articles.title_orig: US diesel prices remain high despite Trump's moves to boost supplies
articles.title_zh: US diesel prices remain high despite Trump's moves to boost supplies
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By Jarrett Renshaw and Nicole Jao
WASHINGTON/NEW YORK, Oct 9 (Reuters) - US diesel prices remain at near-record highs, up 70% since the US-Israeli war on Iran began despite two recent moves by President Donald Trump to boost supplies: pressuring allies to release emergency reserves and ‌expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel.
The wars in Iran and Ukraine have triggered a severe global fuel supply crunch, pushing the average ‌US diesel price to $6.28 a gallon on Friday, according to motorist group AAA.
"Aside from a recession that hammers consumption, the only thing that can prevent oil prices from rising further and ​put them on a sharp downward trajectory is a durable end to conflicts in the Arabian Gulf and between Russia and Ukraine," said Bob McNally, president of Rapidan Energy Group. "Otherwise, policy options range from marginal to counterproductive."
High fuel prices have made it harder for Trump and his Republican Party to defend narrow congressional majorities in the November 3 midterm elections. The cost of living is the top item cited by voters in a Reuters/Ipsos poll, and high diesel prices put particular ‌pressure on traditional Republican constituencies: farmers, truckers and rural ⁠voters.
Trump's approval rating is at a career-low 32%, according to the poll.
The administration has touted a G7 agreement to release 100 million barrels of oil and petroleum products as a major step to help ease prices, but those barrels ⁠appear to largely cover what remains of a March emergency release by International Energy Agency members, rather than new supply.
A White House official disputed that characterization, saying the earlier commitments were not specifically for refined products. The administration negotiated for the previously committed barrels to be front-loaded with diesel and released on a tight timeline beginning ​immediately, ​the official said.
The White House said Trump was focused on easing temporary disruptions while pursuing ​longer-term energy policies.
The administration's other major initiative, an executive ‌order allowing red-dyed diesel on public roads through year-end, has drawn limited industry uptake. The fuel is chemically identical to what trucks normally burn but is tinted to show it is exempt from the 24.4-cent-per-gallon federal highway tax.
The order defers the federal tax and waives penalties for burning off-road fuel on highways. But major retailers and marketers remain wary of selling it because of unclear tax liabilities, logistical hurdles and the risk of fines when trucks cross state lines.
The tax savings are relatively small with diesel prices above $6 a gallon.
David Fialkov, who lobbies on behalf of NATSO, a trade group for truck stops ‌and travel centers, said the White House appeared to be encouraging the supply chain to ​sell dyed fuel through channels not traditionally used for highway diesel, but said that most ​reputable retailers and marketers were unlikely to do so.
John Tirado, president ​of New Jersey-based commercial fuel supplier Summa Energy, called the red-dyed diesel plan "a Band-Aid on a much bigger problem."
The White ‌House said more than 4,000 retailers distribute dyed diesel. It ​said Treasury Department guidance will clarify the ​rules, allowing drivers to use it without federal tax or penalty. It said the savings should outweigh any detour costs for truckers seeking the fuel.
"The fundamental problem facing the US is not taxation but an exceptionally tight global market for refined products," said Caspian Conran, lead economist ​at Baringa, citing disruptions to energy flows from the ‌Middle East and reduced refining output elsewhere.
He described the measures as short-term steps ahead of the election that could provide "probably a few ​weeks of relief," rather than a durable solution.
(Reporting By Jarrett Renshaw in Washington, Additional reporting by Nicole Jao in New York ​and Timothy Gardner in Washington; Editing by Nathan Crooks, David Gregorio, Rod Nickel)

articles.title_orig: One World Community Health Center hosts free health fair in Omaha
articles.title_zh: One World Community Health Center hosts free health fair in Omaha
articles.content_orig:
By Hannah Nazarenus , News intern
Oct. 9, 2026, 10:48 a.m. ·
One World Community Health Center will host a free, family-friendly health fair Saturday at the South Omaha Campus of Metropolitan Community College as part of Binational Health Week.
The event is open to anyone, regardless of insurance status or whether they are a One World patient, said Vivian Garcia, outreach manager at One World. The fair runs 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.
“Right now, we can see that there's a lot of families that are struggling to even cover that extra cost that insurance doesn't cover,” Garcia said. “So that’s the reason why we invite everyone. It doesn't matter if you have health insurance, if you don't have health insurance.”
Garcia said they expect more than 400 people, up from last year, when attendance was still recovering after COVID-19 forced the events to pause.
“It’s not about getting more patients for a clinic,” Garcia said. “It’s about getting these resources and getting education out in a community.”
Visitors can get cholesterol, blood sugar and blood pressure checks. Specialty services include dermatology, hearing and vision screenings, and basic dental screenings for adults and children. This will be the first year the fair offers ear cleanings for people who fail the hearing test.
Vision services have drawn the most interest, Garcia said. This is the second year the fair will offer full vision screenings with glasses prescribed on site.
“The only thing that they're going to be asked is a good address to have those glasses sent over to their home,” Garcia said.
More than 200 people received glasses that way last year.
Garcia said the fair connects attendees to One World and other clinics and organizations in the Omaha area. Participants fill out a short form with no identifying information.
“What we also hear a lot is just navigating the healthcare system overall,” Garcia said. “Knowing how to go into a provider, to the clinic, to set up an initial appointment. Sometimes individuals are maybe just arriving here in Nebraska, and they don't know exactly where to go.”
Binational Health Week is an initiative of the Mexican government, and One World coordinates its events with the Mexican consulate.
The Saturday fair is the last of three October events. One World also held one Oct. 3 at All Care Health Center in Council Bluffs, Iowa, and a women’s night offering breast exams and cancer screenings in partnership with UNMC.
More information on the event and others hosted by One World can be found on its website.

Stacey Adam, a senior clinical officer at the NIH's foundation, told the New York Times that she expects the program to launch in December. In 2024, the UK launched a similar program, called the Cancer Vaccine Launch Pad .

articles.title_orig: Get in the Spotlight With the Line Life Podcast
articles.title_zh: Get in the Spotlight With the Line Life Podcast
articles.content_orig:
A few years ago, I partnered with Danielle Blanchette and our team from T&D World to launch the  Line Life Podcast. Our mission was simple: to bring the stories from the pages of T&D World magazine to the airwaves.
Due to the nature of their jobs, lineworkers are not in an office working behind a computer day in and day out. Instead, they are slipping on their work boots, packing their tool bags and heading out in the field to keep the power flowing to the customers in their service territories.
Because lineworkers spend a lot of time traveling from one location to the next in their bucket trucks, we wanted to give them a way to listen to our field-focused Electric Utility Operations (EUO) stories on the go.
We started with only audio stories, and then we started branching out into interview-style episodes. For the last few years, I've recorded interviews with lineworkers and their loved ones for future episodes of the Line Life Podcast.
With the 2026 International Lineman's Rodeo Week only a few days away, we're excited to offer that opportunity again to the Lineman's Rodeo attendees. Swing by the T&D World Booth #001 (in the breezeway between the ballroom and the exhibit hall) to sit down with me, Amy Fischbach, for a conversation about your career in the line trade.
I air interview-style episodes on the first and third Fridays of each month and audio stories on the second and fourth Fridays on Podbean and in your favorite podcasting app.
To see all the episodes we've recorded over the years, go to linelife.podbean.com . You can also check out our new International Lineman's Rodeo Roundup page on our T&D World website to see the past Rodeo-related episodes.
I look forward to seeing you during the 2026 International Lineman's Rodeo and putting you in the spotlight for the Line Life Podcast!

articles.title_orig: Real-world study shows positive results for Dupixent regardless of skin color
articles.title_zh: Real-world study shows positive results for Dupixent regardless of skin color
articles.content_orig:
Real-world research using the PEDISTAD registry makes up for the gap left by relatively low enrollment of children with skin of color in the pivotal trials of Dupixent (dupilumab).
Atopic dermatitis is commonly diagnosed in childhood and especially among young children, those under the age of 6. Topical treatments, such as topical corticosteroid creams and calcineurin inhibitors, remain an important part of the armamentarium, but biologics, especially Dupixent (dupilumab), have come on strong as a treatment choice. Clinical trials have led to FDA approvals for, first, adolescents, then young children and finally, infants and toddlers.
But there is a problem with those clinical trials. The prevalence of atopic dermatitis is higher in people with non-White skin compared with those of European ancestry, but the majority of those enrolled in the clinical trials have been White patents.
“We just have too few [people with skin of color] in our clinical trials,” says Amy S. Paller, M.D., chair of the Departments of Dermatology at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine in Chicago and lead investigator of several of the pivotal trials of Dupixent as treatment for atopic dermatitis in children.
A race and ethnic mismatch between individuals enrolled in important clinical trials and those with disease being studied occurs in many areas of medicine. In dermatology, the Skin of Color Society, the National Medical Association Dermatology Section and the National Psoriasis Foundation have launched efforts to increase enrollment of people with skin of color. Last year, the lead investigators of the VISIBLE trial assessing Tremfya (guselkumab) as a treatment for psoriasis published an article in JAMA Dermatology describing their efforts to enroll and retain study participants with skin of color. Their strategies included consulting with a dermatologist with experience treating underrepresented populations, using objective measures of skin tones, using color-polarized photography to better erythema, and using census and claims data to identify study sites.
Although it is too late to redo the clinical trials of Dupixent, Paller and her colleagues have attempted to address the underrepresentation problem with analysis of retrospective real-world research, which uses data collected on patients after a drug or another type of intervention has been introduced into clinical practice.
PEDISTAD (which stands for PEDIatric Study in Atopic Dermatitis) is a 10-year observational study that has enrolled children younger than 12 with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis who had been treated with or are candidates for systemic treatment with biologics, cyclosporine, methotrexate, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, Janus kinase inhibitors, corticosteroids, phototherapy or topical treatment. The study is funded by Sanofi and Regeneron, the companies that developed Dupixent.
In an article published late last month in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology , Paller and her colleagues shared the results of an analysis that included up to four years of follow-up data collected for PEDISTAD. The article comes approximately four years after Paller led another PEDISTAD study that included roughly three years of follow-up. A total of 1,342 patents 12 years and younger had been recruited to participate in the PEDISTAD registry when Paller and her colleagues conducted this study, but only a small fraction (7.4%, or 99 children) had been followed for the full four years.
For this analysis, the researchers compared 240 children who were treated with Dupixent with the 125 who were treated with methotrexate and 135 who were treated with cyclosporine. Of those treated with Dupixent, 93 (39%) were non-White and 147 were White (61%). They categorized patients on an intention-to-treat basis. Because this was a real-world study, treatment was decided by clinicians in consultation with a child’s caregiver, not by randomization according to a study protocol. Patients were categorized by the first treatment they were given, even if they switched to a different treatment later. Race and ethnicity were determined by self-identification and grouped for the analysis in a binary fashion into White and non-White.
Paller and her colleagues looked at a number of different outcomes, including the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI), the percentage body surface area (BSA), the Worst Scratch Numeric Rating Scale (WS-NRS) and the Peak Pruritus Numeric Rating Scale (PP-NRS) that are commonly used in dermatology studies. They also analyzed data collected on a number of quality-of-life measures.
With so many outcomes, three different treatments and the White and non-White comparison, the results of the analysis as reported by Paller and her colleagues are complicated. But the result that they emphasized in the discussion of the article is that the patients treated with Dupixent experienced the largest improvement on many of the important measures — EASI, BSA, PP-NRS, WW-NRS — regardless of skin color. They also note the lower discontinuation rate among the children treated with Dupixent.
“In this analysis of real-world data from the PEDISTAD Registry, dupilumab appears to provide consistent disease control irrespective of skin color,” is the summary statement from Paller and her colleagues in the discussion section of the paper. In a brief interview with Managed Healthcare Executive , Paller said of the result, “It was hoped for” and called it “reassuring.”

articles.title_orig: Hack the World: Why hackathons are still the best place to learn to build
articles.title_zh: Hack the World: Why hackathons are still the best place to learn to build
articles.content_orig:
Someone bursts through the door and announces, “There’s pizza!” Nearby, a team has duct tape and cardboard holding its prototype together. Another is debugging a model that won’t detect their movements.
This is a common scene during hackathons, and for a lot of people they’re the place to learn to build.
During several recent hackathons, we followed dozens of participants from the badge line to final demos and asked them what keeps them coming back.
Teams come up with ideas for robots, apps, websites, hardware, and more, then try to get prototypes working before time runs out.
These aren’t small things, these are big endeavors, and they’re going to try to do it in basically two days.
Yana describes it as two days of intense focus on one small experimental project that moves the needle forward. For Nithya, it’s a rare chance to work as hard as you can on something you’re proud of.
It is basically an invention marathon.
For most of computing history, building software required years of specialized training. Not anymore: with AI-powered tools like GitHub Copilot, natural language is becoming a universal programming language, and anyone with an idea can start turning it into working code.
Lance’s team hit a problem at the very last minute. They needed a news API so people could fact-check the information they were getting.
GitHub Copilot was able to not only create a frontend in 30 minutes but also connects with the actual API itself and integrates it all together.
When they’re paired up with someone that’s a CS major, or when they just go and use AI to start a prototype and convince others to join in on their idea, it’s giving this autonomy for people to do what they’re most passionate about.
Call it a learning event, Jon says, and people might not want to go. But tell them there’s pizza, and they’ll show up anyway, and they’ll still end up learning.
Jon calls it the best educational experience you can get as a technologist. Sarvesh puts it more simply: it’s a better way to learn.
Eric calls hackathons a huge grind of continuous work and continuous debugging. Vaishnavi’s team spent part of the time fighting a model that couldn’t detect their movements. “Like, nothing is working,” Vaishnavi said at one point. Mayank’s team got there through trial and error, with duct tape and cardboard.
Hackathons are a safe third place. It’s okay to fail and experiment. You’re not going to get an F, you’re not going to get fired over it.
Niels once searched Google to find out who came up with the term “hackathon,” and his own name came up. He doesn’t remember coining it, but he does remember setting laptops down wherever there was space, sleeping on the floor in sleeping bags, and going straight back to hacking after waking up.
If you feel you have to do it and you don’t like the people around you, then you’re missing the point.
Akankshya found everyone open to collaborating and never felt pushed to quit or leave. Shehmeer could turn to the person on either side and ask how to do something. If they didn’t know, they usually knew someone there who did.
My first hackathon, I met two guys that are now my best friends.
When you meet someone who you bond with over a shared interest, that’s a friendship of practice.
Mike’s first hackathon changed the course of his career:
At my first hackathon, I learned more in one weekend than I had in my entire university degree up to that point.
The next day, Mike looked in the mirror and told himself to forget being a lawyer and become a hacker.
Lee has seen hackathons act as a bridge between the spark of an idea and something rolled out into production. Shehmeer says organizers are trying to show a new generation that building isn’t out of reach.
For Yana, seeing the work happen pulls more people in, because there’s now a bit more of an open door.
You can solve problems yourself, you don’t have to ask someone else for permission.
Everyone is welcome. Student or professional. All identities. All abilities. All backgrounds. All experience levels.
Join us on GitHub. Let’s build something together.
Learn to direct AI agents, critically review their output, and keep technical judgment at the center of your workflow.
Developers are owning more of the delivery system around code, not just code itself. Join us during GitHub Universe to meet other devs, learn something new, and explore what’s next.
Learn how I modernized an old codebase of mine using stacked sessions and pull requests in the GitHub Copilot app.
Discover tips, technical guides, and best practices in our biweekly newsletter just for devs.
