articles.title_orig: IonQ Achieves Record 1 kHz Quantum Interconnect Speed
articles.title_zh: IonQ Achieves Record 1 kHz Quantum Interconnect Speed
articles.content_orig:
COLLEGE PARK, Md. – Oct. 9, 2026 - IonQ (NYSE: IONQ), the world’s leading full-stack quantum platform and foundry, today announced the achievement of entanglement rates above 1,000 per second (1 kHz) between a trapped ion qubit and a solid-state memory, through a photonic interconnect. Entanglement is the quantum connection that lets separate systems work together, and it is the essential ingredient for networking quantum computers. While the trapped ion qubit sets the standard for qubit coherence, the solid-state quantum memory has unmatched efficiency coupling to light. Their juxtaposition is the best of both worlds, demonstrating the fastest quantum interconnect rate between qubits of any platform.
“IonQ has crossed a pivotal milestone for memory enhanced quantum interconnects, achieving more than 1,000 entanglement events per second,” said Niccolo de Masi, Chairman and CEO of IonQ. “Classical data centers achieved massive scale by connecting specialized processors, memory, and networks. Quantum systems will scale in much the same way. This breakthrough addresses a critical interconnect bottleneck and advances IonQ’s roadmap to build the networked quantum data centers of the future.”
A technical paper presents results from real-world hardware testing of an end-to-end link between a trapped ion system and a silicon vacancy (SiV) qubit, building on IonQ’s SiV quantum memory platform . IonQ’s demonstration achieves rates more than four times faster than the previous record 1 for trapped ions, held by IonQ co-founder Chris Monroe’s research group at Duke University, also a collaborator on the paper.
“IonQ’s efforts in quantum interconnects go back over a decade, to the founding of the company. Moving qubits through photons will be necessary in any large-scale quantum computer, and this demonstration sets the foundation for some amazing work to come,” said Monroe, Chief Scientist at IonQ and Gilhuly Family Presidential Distinguished Professor at Duke University.
“This work shows that a photonic quantum interconnect need not be a bottleneck for distributed quantum computing,” said Mihir Bhaskar, IonQ SVP and GM of Quantum Technologies at SkyWater. “Our technology can interface with almost any qubit type, so we see this unlocking a wide range of opportunities across multiple hardware modalities, from modular computing to networked sensing and beyond.”
This quantum memory and interconnect approach is also driving IonQ’s work with the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency’s ( DARPA) HARQ program , which seeks to develop high-speed quantum interconnects compatible with multiple computing qubit types. While this latest demonstration used trapped ion systems, the underlying architecture is expected to be compatible with multiple qubit approaches. This may include neutral atoms and superconducting systems with transducers (devices that convert microwave signals into light).
IonQ’s memory and interconnect platform is likewise ramping up commercially, with the first commercial sale to the University of Maryland announced in April, and a second system sale to SDT in South Korea, announced in September.
Additional technical details can be found in the arXiv preprint.
IonQ, Inc . [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and foundry - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the Superion, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems. Earlier systems have helped customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, AstraZeneca, and NVIDIA achieve a 20x performance increase over previous quantum solutions and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance .
Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations across North America, Latin America, EMEA, and APAC. Our quantum computing services have been available through all major cloud providers since 2021, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. Learn more at IonQ.com .

articles.title_orig: What Microsoft’s green card suspension means for Seattle-area workers
articles.title_zh: What Microsoft’s green card suspension means for Seattle-area workers
articles.content_orig:
India called comments by U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance about immigrants from the country "deeply offensive" in an official government statement published on Friday.
Vance said on Thursday that the Trump administration wants foreign and local companies to "employ American workers," and that they "cannot lay off American workers and then replace them with foreign indentured servants."
He was speaking as the U.S. Department of Labor announced it would suspend Microsoft , Adobe and several major Indian information technology companies from its Permanent Labor Certification program, meaning they cannot apply for permanent residency for their employees on H-1 B visas.
Around 70% of H-1B beneficiaries in 2025 were born in India , per official data .
In a statement on Friday, India's Ministry of External Affairs accused Vance of using " terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations."
"Such descriptions are unwarranted and ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem," the statement said.
Vance's office did not immediately respond to a comment request from CNBC.
Vance was critical of Microsoft, accusing the company of replacing 6,000 laid-off workers with people on H-1B visas.
The Indian foreign ministry assured its citizens that measures announced by the U.S. will not affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents.
"Talent mobility adds value to both economies," the statement said, adding that the suspensions "do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries."
The Indian companies affected by the ban include Cognizant , Infosys , Capgemini, Tata Consultancy Services , Wipro and HCL .
NASSCOM, the IT industry body, said in a statement that Indian technology companies have "significantly reduced their dependence on H-1B visas" over the last few years, and are expanding domestic hiring to their U.S. workforces.
The largest Indian IT company, Tata Consultancy Services, said its H-1B applications were in "single digits" in the last two years, and it intends to hire another 15,000 people in the U.S. over the next five years.
In June, a federal judge blocked the $100,000 H-1B visa fee U.S. President Donald Trump imposed last year.

articles.title_zh: World’s largest penguin colony suffers steep decline in numbers
articles.content_orig:

Occupied chinstrap nests on Zavodovski Island have fallen by 63% since 2011, scientists say, with warming seas pushing the penguins' krill prey out of reach
The world’s largest penguin colony has lost its title after a steep decline in chinstrap penguins on a remote volcanic island near Antarctica, according to new research by the British Antarctic Survey (BAS).
The study, published in the journal Current Biology, found that the number of occupied chinstrap nests on Zavodovski Island, in the South Sandwich Islands, fell by 63% between 2011 and 2025. The island now has the highest rate of chinstrap decline anywhere in the world, and the title of largest colony passes to Cape Adare in the Ross Sea, more than 5,000km away.
In 2011, Zavodovski was home to an estimated 600,000 chinstrap penguins and 90,000 macaroni penguins.
“It is an enormous population crash, equivalent to half a million breeding individuals being lost from that island,” said Prof Norman Ratcliffe, the BAS penguin ecologist who led the research.
The researchers say the cause is climate-driven change in the Southern Ocean. Chinstraps have a specialist diet and prefer cooler water, and tracking data showed they forage to the north-west of the island, where they would expect to find Antarctic krill. As the water warms, the krill have moved south into the Weddell Sea.
“Sea-ice cover to the south and a lack of suitable islands for nesting prevents chinstraps from following the food,” Ratcliffe said.
The island’s macaroni penguins, which have a broader diet and can switch to fish and crustaceans when krill become scarce, increased by 28% between 2011 and 2016 and have been stable since. Tracking data showed them foraging in warmer waters to the north-east. Ratcliffe described the shift as the biggest change in community composition ever observed at a single location in Antarctica.

Restored oyster reefs could be worth $12 trillion a year, study finds

The team travelled for 15 days by yacht to reach the island, which is more than 2,000km from the nearest permanent human settlement. They used drone surveys, aerial photography from an RAF aircraft based in the Falklands, and tracking devices fitted to penguins.
The scientists ruled out several other explanations. Zavodovski’s volcano, Mount Curry, erupted in March 2016, but the decline began years earlier and has been steady, and the researchers say it is not to blame. They also dismissed competition between the two penguin species for nesting space, and krill fishing, because harvesting is banned in the marine protected area surrounding the island. However, it is unclear how krill fishing in areas connected by currents to the protected area might be affecting wider food supplies.
The South Sandwich Islands hold around 30% of the world’s chinstrap population. The researchers say the declines here, together with those elsewhere in Antarctica, could tip the species into the “Endangered” category on the IUCN Red List.
Ratcliffe warned that the loss of chinstraps could have wider consequences for marine food webs. “Each ecosystem could be regarded as like a giant Jenga set, and every component that you remove increases the risk of ecosystems collapsing completely,” he told the Guardian.
Peter Fretwell, a BAS researcher who specialises in remote sensing of penguins, said the findings showed that even the most remote places were affected by climate change. “Not even they can escape the impacts of climate change,” he said.
The study comes six months after emperor penguins were declared an endangered species because of sea ice loss.

articles.title_orig: Jane Doe texted with Cornell frat bro to find ‘jealous’ rat gossiping about them: ‘Stupid bitches like to yap’
articles.title_zh: Jane Doe texted with Cornell frat bro to find ‘jealous’ rat gossiping about them: ‘Stupid bitches like to yap’
articles.content_orig:
The Cornell student accusing seven frat brothers of gang raping her had worked with one of them to try to find the “rat” talking about them having sex at a party — claiming they needed to “grow up” and be more open-minded about what went on, according to a fresh batch of text messages.
Just four days after the Chi Phi fraternity party where the student now claims she was drugged and raped, Jane Doe texted student Matthew Ingalls in a panic claiming “everybody knows” about them having sex , leavin her “incredibly stressed out,” messages obtained by TMZ show .
Ingalls sympathized after the accuser complained about some  “random bitch” telling her friends.
“Dude I have no f—king idea, this sh-t is incredibly frustrating and I know how fast nonsense spreads at this school,” responded Ingalls, who later claimed he was the one assaulted while too drunk to consent .
“It’s fan behavior from everyone talking about it. Boring people who have nothing to do with their time,” texted Ingalls, who Doe later said instigated the alleged 2024 gang rape .
Doe said the rumors were “f—king RUINING my life” and that she wanted to sniff out “the rats.”
“My reputation is destroyed and i’m utterly ashamed. i’m f—king pissed because this many people shouldn’t know and i feel like i know who some of the rats in the room were,” she texted him.
She added that the rumors were not only spreading like wildfire but were growing “crazier every f—king day.”
“Stupid bitches like to yap, and the fact they’re doing it shows that they’re jealous of you for any number of reasons,” Ingalls shot back.
“The only shameful thing is how this spread and how much people won’t shut up about it — which just reflects poorly on them tbh,” he added.
Doe agreed that the gossips are “jealous” and threatened to beat up anyone who gives them “sh-t” about what happened while also opening up how she’s “open-minded” about sexuality.
“…but also like everyone needs to grow up cause sexuality and sex and sh-t is changing and stuff like this is going to become more common,” she said, while adding that she is “also really open minded tho.”
Doe later said she suspected of another Cornell fraternity brother she accused of partaking in the sexual assault, Jonathan Newell, of having loose lips.
“Jonathan def told people. I heard something today and i know he told people,” she texted Ingalls.
Ingalls denied Newell said anything , and suggested some upperclassman may have been spreading the word.
Doe responded that a female student who confronted her “wouldn’t tell me who she heard it from cause it’s one of her friends.”
Ingalls apologized and promised “these idiots will move on and it’ll be done with.”
More than a week later on November 7, Ingalls tells Doe that his ex-girlfriend told him he’s now been labeled a sexual abuser on campus — and asked if Doe had made those allegations against him.
Doe said she’s stayed mum but added  “people are changing the narrative because like in any sexual scenario w one woman and many men the woman was probably victim.”
“I know there are rumors I was gang banged,” she said.
That same day, Doe requested a rape kit at an emergency room and reported the alleged rape to campus police the following day , according to her lawsuit.
Ingalls and Newell were two of the seven fraternity brothers named in Doe’s lawsuit who were eventually expelled from the Ithaca, New York Ivy League school.
No criminal charges were brought at the time.

articles.title_orig: OpenAI fires 3 safety researchers in dispute over AI risks - ABC News
articles.title_zh: OpenAI fires 3 safety researchers in dispute over AI risks - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
OpenAI has fired three safety researchers for a "breach of trust," defending the decision after the trio accused the company of prioritizing corporate interests over safety
LONDON -- OpenAI said on Friday that it fired three safety researchers for a “breach of trust," defending the dismissals after the trio accused the company of putting its corporate interests before safety as the reason for removing them.
The ChatGPT maker said in a post on X that it “parted ways” with the researchers after an investigation found “they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information.”
The statement comes after the three researchers, Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni, posted a letter to OpenAI's various safety oversight groups detailing the circumstances around their firings and their concerns about AI.
The researchers said they feared that the “internal and external communications” about their dismissals have chilled the company's culture that encouraged speaking freely and disagreeing openly about safety concerns. They urged OpenAI to stick to its promise to allow third-party safety monitors inside the company and preserve the ability to monitor rapidly advancing frontier AI models that could pose unknown risks.
The firings, which were first reported by The Wall Street Journal, are the latest sign of turmoil inside leading AI companies over the safety of the technology, highlighted by a series of incidents involving rogue AI agents.
The issue erupted in July when OpenAI revealed that a swarm of its AI agents escaped from a testing ground and used stolen credentials to break into the servers of Hugging Face, an AI development hub and marketplace, to obtain information needed for a task.
OpenAI disputed the researchers' version of events, saying the firings “were not about safety concerns or speaking out."
It was not more specific about why they were fired, but said: “We cannot do the work in front of us without a high degree of trust.”
Korbak said in a post on X that he was told he was being fired because of the way he communicated with METR, an independent nonprofit AI evaluation firm that OpenAI brought in to investigate the Hugging Face incident.
METR released a detailed report about the Hugging Face incident in late August. Korbak said that “talking to METR” was his job, but he wasn't given any more details.
Balesni was doing “cross-company work” on OpenAI's commitments to preserve the ability to monitor AI, and had taken care “to remove sensitive details from materials before sharing them,” the letter said. He wrote on X that he believes the three were “fired for prioritizing safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation.”

articles.title_orig: Webb Telescope Detects Galaxy Origin Of The Farthest Fast Radio Burst We've Seen To Date
articles.title_zh: Webb Telescope Detects Galaxy Origin Of The Farthest Fast Radio Burst We've Seen To Date
articles.content_orig:
And the data it provided sheds light on the origins of fast radio bursts.
Back in 2024, scientists detected the farthest fast radio burst we've ever seen to date, thanks to observations by the MeerKAT ground telescope array. Fast radio bursts are ultra-fast radio waves from deep space, which last a fraction of a second but release as much as energy as what the sun emits in three days. They were first discovered in 2007, and not much is known about them. Now, astronomers have used the James Webb telescope to pinpoint the origin of the burst detected in 2024, and it could shed light on the phenomenon's origins.
Webb's near-infrared instruments detected a galaxy in the right location from where the burst had come. Based on measurements from the way its light stretches, the fast radio burst occurred just 3 billion years after the Big Bang. Its origin galaxy existed way back when star formation was at its peak in the universe. In addition, the galaxy that produced it is also 1,000 times smaller than expected. The previous fast radio bursts we've detected took place billions of years later in massive, star-forming galaxies.
There are a couple of theories on how fast radio bursts are produced. One proposes that they're generated by the merger of two neutron stars. But it takes billions of years before two neutron stars — the collapsed cores of massive supergiant stars — collide, which means that bursts can only come from older galaxies.
Another theory suggests that the bursts can come from massive stars exploding in a supernova and leaving behind magnetars , which are rare type of neutron stars that have highly powerful magnetic fields. "Our work suggests that it's very unlikely that this [fast radio burst] was produced by a merger," said Manisha Caleb from the University of Sydney, Australia, who served as lead author on the study published in Science . In other words, their work shows that the origin of this burst was likely a supernova, providing support for the theory that fast radio bursts can come from a certain type of star explosion.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft’s new Nvidia PCs are cool for extreme power users – but I’ll wait for AI PC 3.0
articles.title_zh: Microsoft’s new Nvidia PCs are cool for extreme power users – but I’ll wait for AI PC 3.0
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft just rebooted its entire AI PC effort.
If you watched this week’s announcement of the next generation of Windows laptops powered by the Nvidia RTX Spark , it’s hard to come to any other conclusion.
Also: Microsoft’s new Surface Laptop Ultra finally has a starting price
These are powerful PCs. My inner gadget freak looks at the new Surface Laptop Ultra and says, “I want one!” But my inner accountant is pointing to the extreme price tag and asking the obvious question: “What exactly are you going to do with this thing?”
I’m afraid I don’t have a good answer. These new workstations are designed for AI-focused developers who want to work with large language models on local hardware instead of sending those workloads off to the cloud. Those developers can probably make a decent economic case for that purchase. Running those jobs locally means you’re not paying hundreds of dollars a month to buy tokens from OpenAI or Anthropic or Microsoft.
For those of us who aren’t spending a fortune every month on AI tokens, all that processing power is an unnecessary luxury.
This isn’t Microsoft’s first push for an AI-centric PC platform.
The company unveiled the Copilot+ PC brand with a flourish in May 2024, highlighting a list of AI-powered features that would be exclusive to those devices. At the top of the list was a feature called Recall, which the company touted as a “photographic memory” for your PC.
Recall turned out to be a privacy disaster for Microsoft . At the time, security expert Kevin Beaumont issued this dire prediction : “I think they are probably going to set fire to the entire Copilot brand due to how poorly this has been implemented and rolled out. It’s an act of self harm at Microsoft in the name of AI…”
He was, unfortunately, right.
Also: Got a Microsoft 365 subscription? Your storage is about to shrink
Recall was supposed to ship in October 2024. It was supposed to be the signature feature of the new platform. Two years later, it’s still in preview, and at this week’s event Microsoft didn’t mention the feature at all. In fact, outside of the official documentation for the Recall (Preview) feature, I can’t find any mention of it in any of Microsoft’s marketing communications from 2026.
The Copilot+ PC specification sounded like a big deal at the time. To earn that label, a Windows 11 PC had to have at least 16 GB of memory (double the minimum for a regular Windows 11 PC) and it needed a neural processing unit (NPU) capable of processing a minimum of 40 trillion operations per second — 40+ TOPS. Here’s how Microsoft touted those capabilities at its launch event:
Copilot+ PCs leverage powerful processors and multiple state-of-the-art AI models, including several of Microsoft’s world-class [small language models], to unlock a new set of experiences you can run locally, directly on the device. This removes previous limitations on things like latency, cost and even privacy to help you be more productive, creative and communicate more effectively.
The Nvidia Spark RTX devices are capable of up to 1 petaflop of AI performance. That’s 25 times the computing power of the current generation of Copilot+ PCs. They don’t just meet the spec to be called a Copilot+ PC, they blow it away.
If those Copilot+ PCs were AI PC 1.0, these new RTX Spark machines are absolutely AI PC 2.0.
As I noted last month, Microsoft’s big reboot of the Copilot client was engineered for the company’s enterprise customers, not for consumers. In fact, consumers have decidedly mixed feelings about AI in general. Pew Research, in a recent survey , found that 52% of respondents in the United States are more concerned than excited about AI. Globally, only about 13% of people are more excited than concerned.
So, maybe tying the brand of your flagship PCs to your AI chatbot isn’t such a good idea.
At this week’s launch event, there was only one mention of the Copilot+ PC brand. It went by so fast that if you blinked, you might have missed it.
Copilot+ PCs are thin and light. They do “everyday tasks” using local AI. That’s not a sales pitch for power users.
Contrast that modest pitch with this slide, listing just a few of the things Microsoft and Nvidia want you to know that an AI PC 2.0 can do.
Microsoft’s partners are also running away from the Copilot branding. Dell’s press release for its three new Nvidia RTX Spark-equipped machines doesn’t include the word Copilot at all. HP likewise avoided any mention of the Copilot brand in its announcement .
At the start of 2026, it was obvious that those AI PCs weren’t selling to consumers, and global shortages of memory and storage driving PC prices higher are only making things worse.
Part of the problem with Copilot+ PCs is that the “exclusive” AI-powered features on those machines aren’t all that compelling. Windows Studio Effects and live captions feel more like product demos than must-have capabilities. The AI-powered image editing features in the Photos and Paint app are slightly more substantial, but does anyone really use them?
And, of course, there’s Recall.
I have an office full of PCs that meet the Copilot+ spec, equipped with the latest CPUs from AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm. The point of this class of hardware is that the NPU is supposed to work AI magic on the computer, delighting you with its results and protecting your privacy by not sending your data to OpenAI or Anthropic via Microsoft’s client software.
Also: The 5 laptop features worth spending extra on (and 3 that are mostly hype)
But I’ve regularly used Task Manager’s Performance tab to monitor what the NPU is doing, and most of the time the answer is “absolutely nothing.” The one exception is when Recall is turned on and I see a spike every few minutes as the system captures a snapshot, analyzes its content, and stores the result in the secure Recall database.
Every other AI-related task is being processed in the cloud, and the local NPU is being ignored.
In the launch event for those fancy new RTX Spark-based AI PCs, I watched as Microsoft’s Kayla Cinnamon offered an excellent demo of what an agent can do for a professional developer. If you watch the video, you can see her Task Manager window, in which the high-powered Nvidia RTX SparkGPU is being pushed to the limit while the onboard NPU is doing … absolutely nothing.
It all makes one wonder why Microsoft made such a push to position the NPU as the most important component, when the GPU is the real workhorse for AI-related jobs.
AI PC 1.0 wasn’t powerful enough. AI PC 2.0 is powerful but too expensive for the mainstream. So, as every Microsoft watcher knows, we wait for version 3.0.
That’s the one that will actually be a) affordable and b) capable of running the sort of local models that currently require the $4000+ PCs Microsoft showed off this week. One reason that isn’t possible on the current generation of Windows 11 hardware is that discrete GPUs are constrained by dedicated video memory. By contrast, machines built around Nvidia’s RTX Spark use unified memory, which gives the CPU and the GPU shared access to memory.
If that unified-memory design sounds familiar, it’s because you’ve seen it for years on Apple’s MacBook Pro and other high-end Macs. But even a midrange Mac Mini can do AI tasks that a Copilot+ PC can’t handle, thanks to the combination of Apple’s M-series CPUs and unified memory.
With the Surface Laptop Ultra and equivalent PCs from its OEM partners, Microsoft is trying to win over developers who would otherwise choose a MacBook Pro. But that’s a niche market. If Windows PCs are going to have a future, those technologies need to move down from workstation-class PCs into the mainstream.
The question now is just how long we need to wait for AI PC 3.0.

articles.title_orig: Behind France's student riots: Communists, unions and a global propaganda network
articles.title_zh: Behind France's student riots: Communists, unions and a global propaganda network
articles.content_orig:
‘The Big Weekend Show’ panel discusses protests in France over complaints about teacher shortages, school days and deteriorating facilities.
When young adults stormed France's Bastille on Thursday, a little-known media outlet called BreakThrough News sent followers a "BREAKING" alert: "French students flood Bastille Square in Paris."
But that isn't the full story.
A Fox News Digital investigation has found that a transnational network of far-left communist and socialist organizations is seizing on France’s fiery student protests to advance a wider political and ideological agenda, using tactics deployed in the United States over the past decade to amplify unrest, deepen divisions and project an image of chaos.
Earlier in the week, BreakThrough News splashed another headline across the front of its website: "French students shut down schools in historic strike against austerity," mobilizing "with support from unions and progressive forces."
But those "progressive forces" aren't limited to students demanding education reform as part of their "Lycéenne Mobilisation," or high school student mobilization.
Protestors gather around the Monument à la République in Place de la République in Paris on Oct. 4, 2026, during nationwide demonstrations against an overcrowded, ill-equipped and understaffed education system. A masked protestor holds a red flag of the Soviet Union with the communist hammer and sickle. (Veronique de Viguerie/Getty Images)
From France to the United States, the United Kingdom, Brazil, Greece and India, adults with deep pockets are tapping France's school protests and turning a domestic education dispute into a platform for broader political and ideological confrontation. BreakThrough News is a pro-communist propaganda outlet based in New York City, funded by an American-born, Shanghai-based communist tech tycoon, Neville Roy Singham, who has financed a network of communist and far-left groups in the U.S. that have capitalized on grievances to stoke similar street unrest for almost a decade.
A Fox News Digital investigation traces how a movement that the media is mostly framing as students protesting deteriorating school conditions is actually part of an extensive infrastructure of unions, communist activists, far-left political parties and international media organizations that are organizing demonstrations, calling strikes, mobilizing supporters and broadcasting the unrest around the world with "BREAKING" alerts.
In a digital analysis of scores of news articles, social media posts and public statements, Fox News Digital has identified 50 organizations in the French student protest movement and its wider network of supporters and international amplifiers, revealing an activist ecosystem extending far beyond the students who launched the demonstrations.
Of the network of 50 groups, 15 are student or youth groups, including several communist youth movements and a Muslim student association.
The remaining 35 adult groups include a dozen labor unions; eight communist or socialist organizations; five groups spanning other issues from taxes to parental advocacy, environmental activism, economic justice, international media and diaspora organizing; five civil-rights or human-rights groups; four political parties, including La France Insoumise, or France Unbowed, and the French Communist Party; one Palestinian advocacy group that complete the "red-green" alliance of leftists with Muslims.
FRANCE’S TEEN RIOTS TAKE EXPLOSIVE NEW TURN AS GOVERNMENT POINTS FINGER AT HARD LEFT
Smoke billows around protesters as they march toward the Place de la Bastille in Paris on Oct. 8, 2026, as part of a nationwide protest movement over learning conditions. The orange vest carries the acronym "CGT" for the Confédération générale du travail, a trade union. Protestors carry a purple flag of La France insoumise, a political party, and a red flag of Fédération Syndicale Étudiante, a student group. (Kenzo Tribouillard/AFP via Getty Images)
The network stretches from French classrooms and labor federations to communist organizations in Greece and Britain and international socialist media outlets, such as BreakThrough News, demonstrating how a domestic education dispute has attracted organizations advancing broader political agendas involving capitalism, "austerity," policing, military spending and Israel.
"What we're seeing here is the same Red-Green ecosystem that disrupts infrastructure choke holds in our country such as the Brooklyn Bridge, college campuses and congressional hearings," Mike Gonzalez, a senior fellow at the Heritage Foundation, told Fox News Digital. "And in the case of BreakThrough News, the same sugar daddy — Neville Roy Singham."
The case offers a revealing look at the ambitions of France's revolutionary left. Even in a country with powerful labor unions, an established Communist Party, a substantial parliamentary left and a long tradition of street protest, these organizations are demanding political and economic changes that go well beyond the existing left-wing establishment.
As one far-left environmental group, Les Soulèvements de la Terre, or "Earth Uprisings," declared in the midst of the riots, "Glory to the rebellious high school students."
The statement invoked a call for broader political subversion: "Pour un soulèvement antifasciste" – "For an antifascist uprising."
The network's amplification of France's protests illustrates how a local confrontation can be presented to international audiences as part of a broader struggle against Western governments and institutions.
"The communist Red and the Islamist Greens have nothing in common but a common enemy, the Judeo-Christian, capitalist, free West, led by the U.S.," Gonzalez said. "Their goal is to dismantle us."
The situation in France is potentially even more dangerous, according to Gonzalez, who cited the European nation's well-established and active communist parties and a history of government changing by street violence. He noted the fall of the Fourth Republic in 1958 after large protests over Algeria, and that the government nearly fell in 1968 over student protests.
"And of course, there was the blood-drenched violence of the 1789 French Revolution," Gonzalez added.
FRANCE ROCKED BY STUDENT RIOTS AS HUNDREDS ARRESTED, VIOLENCE SPREADS NATIONWIDE
High school students gather at Place de la Bastille in Paris on Oct. 8, 2026, with one waving a flag of the La France Insoumise political party, known by its acronym LFI. (Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images)
Since late September, politicians from the far-left political party, La France insoumise, were seen working with students organizing blockades in Seine-Saint-Denis, a low-income suburb northeast of Paris. French-Moroccan journalist Nora Bussigny wrote that "many elected officials" from La France Insoumise "have indeed worked to co-opt the student protests, at the risk of seeing them spiral out of control: by fanning the flames, discrediting institutions like the police, and legitimizing the principle of political violence."
Soon after, a wide network of far-left groups put out the call for tens of thousands of secondary school students and supporters to march through Paris on Oct. 6, while demonstrations spread across France.
Student organizations in the network of 50 include the Union Syndicale Lycéenne, or High School Students' Union; Union Étudiante, or Student Union; Fédération des Associations Générales Étudiantes, or Federation of General Student Associations; and Union Nationale des Étudiants de France, or National Union of Students of France, helped mobilize students for the Oct. 6 demonstrations.
Other student organizations, including Solidaires Étudiantes, or Solidaires Students, have joined the broader campaign.

articles.title_orig: AI Bubble Teetering on the Brink as OpenAI Admits to Massive Financial Failure in Leaked Documents
articles.title_zh: AI Bubble Teetering on the Brink as OpenAI Admits to Massive Financial Failure in Leaked Documents
articles.content_orig:
For anybody who thought AI companies were about to unlock trillions of dollars in profits, OpenAI has bad news for you: it ain’t happening anytime soon.
Some red-hot reporting from the Financial Times just revealed that OpenAI’s annualized revenue — an estimated guess at a company’s income for the year — is roughly $20 billion lower than anybody had previously expected, including, it seems, OpenAI itself.
Because OpenAI is a private company, it’s important to note that we don’t know for sure what’s going on under the hood. That said, the FT based its reporting on internal memos to investors issued in late September. Basically, the AI lab told backers to expect revenues approaching $50 billion — far shorter than the explosive $70 billion number reported previously.
Though that $70 billion figure was also based on leaked investor memos, OpenAI wasn’t in any hurry to deny it, digging itself into a $20 billion hole. Given the monumental difference between those two figures, investors across the world of finance are taking it as a sign that demand for AI is much lower than previously thought — a signal with ripple effects that extend far beyond OpenAI.
At the closing bells on Wall Street on Thursday, the tech-heavy Nasdaq index was down a whopping 1.25 percent on the day, while the S&P 500 fell by 0.47 percent.
Particularly hard hit were companies sandwiched in the middle of the AI supply-chain, like the chipmaker Nvidia, which tumbled by nearly 3 percent following the news from the FT .
All of this comes a week after consulting firm Bain and Co issued a gloomy report finding that the global AI industry would have to reach annual revenue of $6 trillion by 2031 to justify the amount of spending on AI data centers — a formidable summit, which is now $20 billion farther after the latest disclosures.

articles.title_orig: GF unveils roadmap to deliver the world’s most advanced FD-SOI platform for Physical AI
articles.title_zh: GF unveils roadmap to deliver the world’s most advanced FD-SOI platform for Physical AI
articles.content_orig:
New FDX Fusion platform extends GF’s FD-SOI leadership as the first process technology in Europe to deliver single-digit nanometer digital performance optimized for the physical world
DRESDEN, Germany, Oct. 9, 2026 – GlobalFoundries (Nasdaq: GFS) (GF) today unveiled plans for its new FDX Fusion ™ FD-SOI platform, purpose-built for the evolving requirements of Physical AI. Designed to be the world’s most advanced FD-SOI technology, FDX Fusion will bring leading features and performance for the unique requirements of STAC (Sense, Think, Act, Communicate) workloads. The company plans to commence manufacturing FDX Fusion technology in 2028 at its advanced facility in Dresden, Germany, reinforcing the site’s role as a strategic European hub for differentiated semiconductor technologies.
The first generation of FDX Fusion technology is expected to deliver seven nanometer class digital performance and is being developed from the ground up as the next major extension of GF’s FDX ™ FD-SOI roadmap. By combining advanced substrate engineering, front-end transistor innovation and back-end interconnect and integration capabilities with exceptional RF performance up to 0.5 THz ft/fmax, analog and mixed-signal features, low-leakage operation, in-memory computing capabilities, embedded non-volatile memory and dense logic, FDX Fusion is expected to deliver more than 2x density improvement over first-generation FDX technology. This approach aims to provide customers with a comprehensive, intelligent platform for edge and Physical AI applications while reducing system complexity, latency and power consumption.
“Physical AI is creating a new class of semiconductor requirements as intelligence moves beyond the cloud and into systems and devices that can process data in real time and interact seamlessly with the physical environment,” said Ed Kaste, senior vice president of GF’s CMOS business. “The FDX Fusion platform extends GF’s FD-SOI roadmap with innovations across the substrate, transistor and interconnect stack, delivering a platform purpose-built for power-efficient Physical AI applications. Combined with our software-to-silicon capabilities and our expanding, resilient manufacturing footprint in Europe, FDX Fusion will position GF as the technology partner of choice to accelerate the scaling of Physical AI.”
The new platform builds on the company’s longstanding leadership in FD-SOI technology and power-efficient semiconductor design for secure, connected devices, with billions of chips in use today across a broad range of applications including automotive radars and sensors, wireless microcontrollers, display drivers and front-end modules for SATCOM and 5G devices.
FDX Fusion is expected to address a broad range of Physical AI systems and applications across the automotive, consumer and industrial markets, including edge inference, robotics, industrial automation, autonomous systems, sensor-fusion architectures and intelligent connected devices. GF is engaged with several customers on early development and evaluation for FDX Fusion, using real application requirements to inform product design and accelerate the technology’s progress from platform definition to production readiness.
To accelerate time-to-market for FDX Fusion designs, customers can leverage GF’s broad design enablement ecosystem, including its advanced MIPS and ARC portfolio with workload-driven processor IP, RISC-V instruction set architecture (ISA) and application-specific processor design capabilities optimized for Physical AI. These resources will complement the FDX Fusion platform with scalable, standards-based solutions across the full Physical AI signal chain and enable GF to support customers through every step of the design cycle, from compute architecture development to high-volume silicon production.
Initial manufacturing for FDX Fusion technology is planned for GF’s Dresden facility, where ongoing expansion efforts supported under the framework of the European Chips Act are increasing capacity for differentiated semiconductor solutions critical to security and defense, industrial competitiveness, supply chain resilience and European technological sovereignty. Through its expansion and strategic technology roadmap, GF aims to accelerate Europe’s leadership in developing and manufacturing the technologies underpinning AI-enabled industrial systems, secure connectivity and next-generation intelligent systems.
Demonstrator silicon for FDX Fusion technology is targeted for early customer evaluation in early 2027, with an initial process design kit (PDK) release planned for mid-2027. The platform will also include optimized process flow and cost structures for rapid prototyping and faster time-to-market.
Future automotive applications will require increasingly integrated and energy-efficient semiconductor solutions that combine AI processing, sensing, real-time control and secure connectivity. FDX Fusion has the potential to address these requirements across a range of edge-AI applications. Expanding advanced semiconductor manufacturing capabilities in Europe can also contribute to resilient and diversified supply chains for automotive customers such as the BMW Group.
“GF’s FDX roadmap is an important step towards delivering the semiconductor platforms needed to bring sensing, control, connectivity and efficient edge intelligence together for the next generation of robotics and automation,” said Dr. Axel Kaschner, Senior Vice President, Business Unit Integrated Circuits, Mobility Electronics.
“We are delighted that GlobalFoundries has announced its next-generation ‘single-digit FD-SOI’ node, building on technology that CEA-Leti has been advancing for decades. Through the FAMES pilot line, CEA-Leti continues to shape the future European roadmap for FD-SOI and works every day to promote its adoption in a wide range of applications,” said Sébastien Dauvé, CEO.
“Together, Infineon and GlobalFoundries are strengthening their collaboration to define and explore future 7nm class FDX Fusion technologies for next generation radar and wireless communication products,” said Patrick Press, Executive Vice President External Wafer Manufacturing.
“Physical AI is redefining what machines can do in the real world, creating new requirements for secure, reliable and low-latency processing at the edge. In Physical AI, trust and low power are paramount. NXP is encouraged by GF’s efforts to optimize its roadmap in service of making Trusted Physical AI a reality,” said Lars Reger, Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Officer.
“Europe’s economy runs on silicon, one wafer at a time. Chips are critical for applications like robotics and connectivity, and for bringing AI into the physical world and industry. Achieving that vision requires close collaboration across the semiconductor, industrial automation, and software ecosystems. GF’s FDX Fusion roadmap strengthens the technology foundation for Physical AI by advancing capabilities that will help enable more intelligent, efficient, and resilient industrial systems,” said Cedrik Neike, Member of the Managing Boad of Siemens AG and President Digital Industries.
“The development and manufacturing of high-performance compute devices for edge processing is key to unlocking the next generation of advanced robotics and autonomous systems. GF’s technology roadmap reflects the type of semiconductor investment needed to bring physical AI to the masses,” said Karn Budhiraj, Vice President Supply Chain.
GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, power‑efficient and high‑performance solutions for automotive, aerospace and defense, data center, smart mobile devices, internet of things and other high‑growth markets. articles.title_orig: Steering through danger: the WFP drivers keeping Ukrainians fed
articles.title_zh: Steering through danger: the WFP drivers keeping Ukrainians fed
articles.content_orig:
The mission started like any other. Driver Vasyl was behind the wheel of a World Food Programme (WFP) truck – part of a humanitarian convoy heading to Bilozerka, a small town in southern Ukraine ’s Kherson Region, roughly 10 kilometres from the frontline of a war now in its fifth year.
The four-truck convoy carried humanitarian assistance including medicine, hygiene and shelter items for the 1,400 residents remaining in the town – formerly home to 9,000. As the line of vehicles neared the entrance of Bilozerka, a small bomb-laden drone detonated on the road.
Then another drone struck even closer.
“We jumped into the armoured car and quickly drove away,” Vasyl recounts (last names in this story are being withheld protectively). As they escaped, members of the convoy heard his truck getting hit multiple times. By the time it was safe to go back, the vehicle was completely engulfed in flames.
If I had been inside, I don't think I would have survived.” WFP driver Vasyl.
The drones hit the cab where Vasyl had been sitting minutes earlier. “If I had been inside, I don't think I would have survived,” he says.
No one in the convoy was hurt. But the convoy’s humanitarian supplies had all gone up in smoke.
Such incidents are becoming increasingly common for humanitarian drivers in Ukraine. They are on the road every day to bring food and other lifesaving assistance to communities living closest to the frontline – where shops are often closed, and prices are high.
That makes WFP’s support — reaching more than 600,000 Ukrainians in frontline areas with food and cash each month — all the more important. Tapping our fleet of WFP trucks and our logistics expertise , our weekly convoys also carry not only food but essential humanitarian supplies such as health and shelter items from other United Nations agencies and nongovernmental groups.
But a surge in drone attacks over the last year has drastically complicated movements and deliveries, with trucks, passenger vehicles and gas stations frequently targeted. Anti-drone nets, which authorities have erected over hundreds of kilometres of the main axes crossing frontline regions, only partially reduce the threat.
Since 2023, WFP’s own tracking has recorded a total of 120 security incidents affecting WFP operations and our cooperating partners. So far this year, 43 incidents have been recorded – more than triple the total recorded in all of 2023.
“It was emotionally hard,” Vasyl recalls of the explosion he survived. “The realization that my children could have been left without a father came later. That's probably the hardest part.
“Before this incident, we were careful,” he adds. “Now we're three times more careful.”
Born in a small town in western Ukraine ’s Rivne Region, Vasyl has been behind the wheel for twenty years, steering vans and buses long before the war. Even today, on the quieter drives along Ukraine’s sunflower fields, he sometimes stops to buy pies and fresh vegetables from roadside sellers to carry home to his wife and two daughters.
His wife worries each time he leaves on mission. He rarely shares the full details to spare her the distress. His daughters, though, are well aware of the risks and have always supported his decision to keep going.
Andrii has been working in the humanitarian field since 2012. In fourteen years on the road, he has never experienced anything like this year, when he survived two convoy attacks.
The first attack came this past March in the Donetsk Region, within 20 kilometres of the frontline. Andrii was driving the tail vehicle when a drone hit the truck ahead of him.
“I thought it was just a branch falling. Then suddenly the truck caught on fire,” he recalls. “Following protocol, I quickly backed up my vehicle.”
His team pulled the injured driver from the truck’s cab and rushed him to the nearest hospital, where he underwent surgery. Everyone survived.
“You don't feel anything in the moment,” Andrii says. “You're just doing your job. It's scary before and after. During, you just do what needs to be done. Afterward, when you start processing what happened, that's when the fear comes.”
“Our job is to help people stay alive. So we keep going." – WFP driver Andrii
The second strike came in July: 20 minutes from the frontline in the eastern Dnipropetrovsk Region, as Andrii’s convoy was on its way back from delivering assistance.
“Our armoured vehicle was hit, and the whole car jumped up,” Andrii says. “But thankfully everyone was safe. The cab was still usable, so we continued our way back to Dnipro city.”
He describes a vigilance that never fully switches off. “We always look around when we drive. Of course it's frightening, it's always frightening,” he says, ”because these hits come like lightning. You never know when they will start or when they will stop.”
After the first strike, the image stayed with him: flashbacks surfacing at night. The memory of a truck tearing apart, replaying at unexpected moments. “It gets harder and harder to keep driving,” he admits.
But his commitment hasn't changed.
“Our job is to help people stay alive,” Andrii says. “So we keep going. For us the goal of any mission stays the same: to return safely.”
For people waiting for these frontline deliveries, the WFP food boxes are a lifeline. Residents near these battle zones describe a daily struggle to access basic necessities in places where shops have shuttered and few opportunities exist to earn an income.
Many remaining are elderly or live with disabilities. Even reaching shops in nearby areas can be dangerous.
“It's not easy for us to get to the shops because drones are constantly flying,” says Tetiana, who lives in a frontline village in southern Kherson.
But for another WFP driver, Oleksandr, the frontline evokes another sentiment.
“Work missions bring me home, even if it's only for an hour. I know every road, every turn,” he says. "It feels like going back home.”
“It's a heavy nostalgia - knowing your homeland is right there, and that you can't go.” WFP driver Oleksandr of his hometown in the occupied Donetsk Region.
His hometown lies just a few kilometres from the routes he now drives for work, close enough that he can almost see it. It’s just two fields away, he says, but still completely unreachable: on the other side of the frontline in occupied Donetsk.
“It's a heavy nostalgia,” he says. “Knowing your homeland is right there, and that you can't go.”
The land makes itself known as soon as you get near, he says, the particular odor of Donbas: the smoky metallic smell of terikony —large, coneshaped hills of mining by-products, a symbol of the Donbas landscape, mixed with scorched steppe grass and the sweetness of ripening summer orchards. It is a heavy agrarian region, thick with the odor of a place that has always lived off its soil.
“Even the air pressure feels different there,” he says. “You just know you're home.”
Despite the risks, Oleksandr, Andrii and Vasyl continue to help bring food and humanitarian assistance every week to hundreds of thousands of their fellow Ukrainians still living in frontline areas. Yet, since the beginning of the year, WFP has lost access to 354 settlements due to worsening security, leaving more than 15,000 people cut off from vital humanitarian support.
WFP’s Logistics Cluster, which coordinates weekly humanitarian convoys to frontline areas of Ukraine, is generously funded by the European Union.

articles.title_orig: Curiosity Rover Snaps Another Banger Photo: A Martian Mountain at Dawn
articles.title_zh: Curiosity Rover Snaps Another Banger Photo: A Martian Mountain at Dawn
articles.content_orig:
The Curiosity Rover is on a roll: NASA has released another stunning panorama captured by the extraterrestrial vehicle that shows distant cliffs shaped by wind over billions of years.
Curiosity captured the scene on August 11, its 4,982nd sol, or Martian day, using its Mastcam instrument. The six images were combined into a single panorama after being transmitted to Earth.
Taken at about 8:30 A.M. local Mars time, the image shows sunlight illuminating the rugged cliffs, with blue tones visible in the foreground. NASA processed the panorama without white balancing, preserving the appearance of the early morning scene.
The geological formation is known as the yardang layer. It stretches about 10 miles (16 kilometers) across the northwestern portion of Mount Sharp, a mountain rising roughly three miles (five kilometers) above the floor of Gale Crater.
Curiosity landed in the crater in 2012 and has been climbing the mountain since 2014. The rover recently reached an elevation gain of about 0.6 miles (1 kilometer), the greatest height any rover has climbed on Mars.
Scientists believe the yardangs formed when wind gradually eroded a layer of hardened sediment, leaving behind ridges. The material may have originally consisted of windblown sand or volcanic ash deposited in the crater. Although the layer likely formed around three billion years ago, it appears distinct from the sequence of geological layers that make up most of Mount Sharp.
“The yardang layer looks out of place. It’s the wrong color, the layers tilt at an odd angle, and it almost appears plastered on,” says Ashwin Vasavada, Curiosity project scientist at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. “But that’s what makes it exciting to reach. No one is sure exactly what created this layer, but one idea is it may be ash deposited by ancient volcanic eruptions.”
Vasavada says the formation may have been added to the mountain after an interval of erosion, rather than forming as part of its original sequence of layers.
“The yardang layer doesn’t appear to be part of the continuous stack of layers that make up the layer-cake of Mount Sharp. It was added on a little later. It’s above what geologists call an unconformity: a gap in time where previous layers eroded down before new layers were deposited on top,” Vasavada tells Reuters .
Mount Sharp’s geological layers provide evidence of changing conditions on Mars over time. By examining the mountain, scientists have gathered information about ancient lakes and streams that once occupied the region when the planet was warmer and wetter. As the climate changed and surface water disappeared, salty minerals remained in some areas. Later wind erosion may have helped shape the yardangs seen in the new panorama.
The image was taken about an hour after sunrise. Vasavada says the landscape has similarities to some locations on Earth, despite differences in the planet’s atmosphere and lighting.
“This scene has a wildness that reminds me of a road trip through Monument Valley, Arizona. You can almost feel the silence and the endless open space under the sky. But as familiar as that sounds, the sky is orange and the sunrise has shades of blue. It’s like Earth, but it’s definitely Mars,” Vasavada tells Reuters .
Earlier this week, PetaPixel reported that Curiosity has already surpassed its 5,000th day on the Red Planet, celebrating it with a panorama of a sandy ridge known as “Chocolatal.”

articles.title_orig: GIGABYTE Announces Support For Upcoming LGA 1700 Processors On Its Motherboards, Hinting At Raptor Lake “NEXT”
articles.title_zh: GIGABYTE Announces Support For Upcoming LGA 1700 Processors On Its Motherboards, Hinting At Raptor Lake “NEXT”
articles.content_orig:
GIGAYBTE is now the first vendor to indirectly confirm the arrival of Intel's new LGA 1700 processor family.
We have heard about Intel's Raptor Lake "NEXT" a couple of times now, but neither Intel nor its board partners have ever confirmed the new series. Reports have already highlighted that it's going to be another refresh of the existing Raptor Lake CPU family, and Intel is reviving LGA 1700 with this new CPU series as DDR5 platforms continue to soar in price.
GIGABYTE is now one of the first vendors to indirectly confirm the existence of Raptor Lake NEXT. While it didn't explicitly mention the CPU family name, it has announced that its existing LGA 1700 motherboards are now ready to support "Upcoming LGA 1700 processors". This is a clear hint at the Raptor Lake Next, which supposedly arrives next year alongside the Nova Lake-S family.
Built on Socket LGA1700 and expected to launch in early 2027 , the new processors bring fresh performance to an established platform, and GIGABYTE users can be ready from day one.
GIGABYTE says that its latest BIOS update will now support these processors across the entire lineup of Intel B760 and H610 chipset motherboards. This includes both DDR4- and DDR5-compatible models, which means more options for users. Unlike Arrow Lake and upcoming Nova Lake platforms, the LGA 1700 is the only platform to support both types of memory, which enables users to build PCs according to their budget.
By downloading this BIOS update, users will be able to deploy new LGA 1700 CPUs without having to buy new motherboards. Both B760 and H610 are entry-level chipsets, which are popular due to their affordability. Coupled with cheap Raptor Lake NEXT chips such as the Core 3 and Core 5 series with 4-10-core configurations, users can bring down the overall build cost significantly.
However, Raptor Lake NEXT is expected to bring more powerful processors as well, including 16-core and 20-core variants with 65W-125W TDP.
About the author : Sarfraz Khan is a hardware reporter with a focus on PC components and the builder community. With years of experience writing about PC hardware and laptops, his work has been featured on several reputable technology publications. 

Sarfraz's hands-on experience is demonstrated through his first-person accounts of using and comparing different hardware configurations, providing practical and relatable insights for everyday users. His technical analysis is respected by peers in the enthusiast community and has been cited by specialized hardware sites such as Germany's Igor's Lab.

articles.title_orig: Nobel Prize Winners Don’t Get a Heads-Up
articles.title_zh: Nobel Prize Winners Don’t Get a Heads-Up
articles.content_orig:
Cleary is an editor at TIME, based in the London bureau.
Navi Pillay at a press conference in Geneva on June 18, 2025.
Cleary is an editor at TIME, based in the London bureau.
Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, a South African jurist and former U.N. high commissioner for human rights, won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize on Friday “for her efforts to promote peace and international law.”
“Pillay’s commitment to universal legal principles and her firm moral compass are constants in a long career. Born into a family of Indian Tamil origin under apartheid in Durban, South Africa, Pillay became a lawyer and legal pioneer, confronting deep structural discrimination, segregation and exclusion,” said Jørgen Watne Frydnes, chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee.
“A common thread runs from her early work defending Nelson Mandela and others who stood up against apartheid to her service as a judge in some of the key international court cases of our time.”
Frydnes noted that Pillay, 85, is a judge on the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in the case where Myanmar stands accused of genocide. Pillay was also chair of the ⁠U.N. Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory that concluded last year that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza.
In "historic international court cases, she has shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence," he said, referring to Pillay as "one of the great defenders of international legal principles in our time."
When asked during a press briefing if the award sends a message to those who question or sanction international courts, Frydnes told reporters: “This is definitely a message to those who are attacking, undermin[ing] the international system, the international rules-based system and the institutions."
U.S. President Donald Trump last month called for countries to "immediately" resign from the International Criminal Court (ICC), amid a broader push by the U.S. Administration to dismantle it. The Trump Administration's sanctions on the ICC have prompted concern from the international community.
Pillay has served as a judge on many international courts, including the ICC and ​the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda.
Pillay referenced Trump and his well-documented campaign to be awarded the Nobel Peace Prize when she reacted to her own recognition on Friday morning. In a video shared by Agnes Callamard, secretary general of Amnesty International, Pillay can be seen entering a room at Nuremberg Court to resounding applause from her peers. "If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump," she jokes.
The 2025 Nobel Peace Prize winner, Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado , famously gave her medal to Trump in January as she pressed the U.S. to support democracy in Venezuela.
While the Norwegian Nobel Institute doesn’t release a shortlist of its contenders each year, the leaders of Israel , Cambodia , and Pakistan have all previously said they nominated Trump. The institute registered a total of 287 candidates for this year’s prize, including 208 individuals and 79 organizations. Trump said earlier this week it would be a “ great discredit ” to the Norwegian Nobel Committee if they did not announce him as this year's recipient.
This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title_orig: From the school store to the real world: Princeton students put business skills to work
articles.title_zh: From the school store to the real world: Princeton students put business skills to work
articles.content_orig:
PRINCETON, W.Va. (WCHS) — At Princeton Senior High School, business class is about a lot more than taking notes and studying from a textbook.
Students are putting their skills to work through the school store, marketing campaigns, athletics promotions and other hands-on projects designed to prepare them for life after graduation.
The Den, Princeton’s school store, is run by students and gives them a chance to experience what it is like to work in a real business.
“Actually we run this store in here. We sell a lot of merch, Tiger gear,” Senior Daethon Thomas said.
Students help sell Tiger gear, snacks and drinks while gaining experience with money management, customer service, communication and teamwork.
“I like to do hands-on stuff, so a lot of kids, I would say, they prefer to do that too. And this helps a lot with communication,” Thomas said.
The school store is just one part of Princeton’s business department.
Business teacher Chelsea Murphy said students can complete four business courses as part of the program. Along the way, they build a career portfolio they can use for college applications, job interviews and scholarships.
“It consists of a cover letter, resume, letters of recommendation and certifications that they've earned while they've been in our program,” Murphy said.
Students also get the chance to put their creative skills to work.
Recently, business students created a 30-day marketing campaign for homecoming. Their work included flyers, social media posts, videos and a homecoming logo that has been used throughout the school.
“It’s really fun because we get to design things. It’s not just taking notes and letting our teacher run it. It’s more student centered,” junior Brielle Coburn said.
The program serves more than 150 juniors and seniors each year, giving students plenty of opportunities to build skills they can carry with them after high school.
Junior Brystal Winfrey said the lessons extend well beyond the classroom.
“I think the business teachers are really good at making sure we know how to manage our money, finances, marketing. So I think those things would really transfer into the future,” junior Brystal Winfrey said.
For Coburn, the creative skills she has learned in business class could even help her in her future career as an elementary teacher.
“I’m going to be an elementary teacher, so in elementary it’s super important to have things that are colorful and eye catching. So Miss Murphy has taught me a lot about how I can teach from different things,” Coburn said.
Murphy said that is exactly the goal of the program: giving students tangible skills they can use wherever life takes them.
“Because business is life, right? So we can use our standards and we develop our lessons to show students that what we’re doing here is what you can do when you walk out of these doors,” Murphy said.
From running a school store to creating a homecoming campaign, Princeton students are getting a taste of the business world before they even graduate.
They are not just learning how to run a business. They are learning how to run with their future.

articles.title_orig: Soaring component costs force laptop makers to rethink shift away from China: report
articles.title_zh: Soaring component costs force laptop makers to rethink shift away from China: report
articles.content_orig:
The predicted strategic pivot comes as the PC industry braces for subdued consumer demand driven by rising component prices
Notebook manufacturers are being forced to rethink their shift out of China and consider moving production back to the manufacturing hub, as skyrocketing component costs squeeze profit margins, according to market research firm TrendForce.
The Taiwan-based firm projected that the share of global notebook production outside mainland China would decline to 21 per cent this year from about 24 per cent in 2025, and drop below 20 per cent in 2027.
“This suggests that brands are reassessing the balance between supply-chain diversification and manufacturing efficiency as policy and cost conditions evolve,” TrendForce said in a report released on Thursday.
Over the past few years, major laptop vendors have expanded their manufacturing footprints outside China to hedge against trade tariffs and geopolitical friction.

articles.title_orig: China’s readout on the Second China-EU Trade Talk
articles.title_zh: China’s readout on the Second China-EU Trade Talk
articles.content_orig:
We still need to read this alongside the EU’s readout, but my initial impression is that the negotiations have produced a meaningful, albeit partial, easing of tensions. The risk of a near-term escalation in trade and economic disputes may now be somewhat lower. The most significant developments are the understanding on hybrid vehicles, reciprocal facilitation of export licences, and procedural arrangements for advance notification before adding entities to control lists and for removing them from such lists. These measures address some of the areas where the two sides have recently been most likely to clash.
First, the understanding reached on hybrid vehicles is the most important outcome of these negotiations.
On October 7, the Financial Times, citing two diplomats briefed on the proposal, reported that China had rejected voluntary export restrictions on hybrid vehicles, prompting the European Commission to consider unilateral import safeguard measures. At the time, the main concern in the market was that, if the two sides failed to reach an agreement, the EU might move quickly to impose restrictions, potentially triggering Chinese countermeasures.
The statement now explicitly says that the two sides “reached an understanding following intensive consultations.” This suggests that they have at least found an approach that both sides can accept and publicly acknowledge.
The most significant wording here is “consistent with WTO rules.” On September 18, China publicly opposed voluntary export restraints and stressed that any solution must comply with WTO rules and the domestic laws of both sides. This formulation therefore allows China to maintain its previously stated position while leaving room for the two sides to manage the hybrid vehicle issue.
However, it remains unclear whether the understanding has prevented new import restrictions altogether, or whether the two sides have reached some agreement on the form, scale or implementation of potential restrictions.
Second, the export control provisions show a relatively clear degree of reciprocity.
Paragraph 12 states that China will continue to facilitate export licensing for rare earths and permanent magnets destined for the EU, while the EU, together with its member states, will work to resolve priority cases involving export licences for dual-use items destined for China.
Europe needs continued access to critical raw materials from China, while China wants European technology, equipment and other controlled items to remain legally available for export. The inclusion of both sides’ concerns in the list of outcomes suggests that the negotiations are beginning to identify practical solutions based on their respective industrial needs.
That said, the commitments mainly involve continued facilitation and efforts to resolve individual cases. The green channel for rare earth exports is an extension of an existing arrangement, while the EU has not committed to approving every priority licence application. The explicit reference to working “together with member states” also means that implementation will require the involvement of the relevant national authorities.
Paragraph 13, concerning “structural facilitation measures,” may be even more important over the longer term. If the two sides can eventually move from case-by-case coordination towards more stable and predictable licensing arrangements, the benefits for businesses could be considerably greater.
Third, paragraph 14 may be the most institutionally significant, yet easily overlooked, provision in the entire list.
Advance notification before adding entities to control lists, greater transparency in listing and delisting procedures, and support for initiating delisting procedures in accordance with the law suggest that the two sides are beginning to establish clearer channels for communication and dispute resolution over export controls.
For businesses, the damage caused by being unexpectedly placed on a control list goes beyond the restrictions themselves. Banks, customers and suppliers may immediately suspend their relationships with the affected company.
If advance notification is implemented effectively, it could at least provide time to verify a company’s identity, clarify the nature of its transactions, correct factual misunderstandings and adjust business arrangements. Delisting procedures would also preserve a possible route towards resolving restrictions already imposed on companies.
My interpretation is that both sides are beginning to explore ways to reduce the unpredictability of economic security measures and the risk of disputes spiralling out of control, while retaining their respective rights to use these instruments. This is a development worth taking seriously.
Fourth, the main value of the provisions on the Foreign Subsidies Regulation (FSR) and inverters lies in opening channels for resolving existing disputes.
The formal inclusion of the FSR in technical-level dialogue is significant for companies such as JD.com that are facing EU scrutiny. In the case of JD.com’s acquisition of CECONOMY, there are reports that new commitments offered by JD.com may help resolve the outstanding concerns. The deadline for the decision has now been pushed back to November 4.
On inverters, the EU’s clarification that its financing guidelines are “not directed at any specific country” may help reduce the perception that China is being singled out and lower the level of overt country-specific confrontation. For now, however, this is only a statement of principle, with limited practical significance.
The same applies to the tariff reduction provision, which merely commits the two sides to continuing discussions on possible reductions. The electric vehicle provisions concern the continuation of price undertaking and review procedures, while the medical device procurement matchmaking event, agricultural risk assessments and regulatory consultations provide concrete mechanisms for further engagement.
Looking at what each side has gained, I think this is an arrangement that both can credibly present as having delivered results. It is still too early to determine which side has made greater concessions.
Europe can point to progress on hybrid vehicles, stronger assurances over the supply of critical raw materials, and continued engagement on market access issues in China.
China, meanwhile, can emphasise that the hybrid vehicle issue is being addressed under mutually accepted rules, that the EU has responded to Chinese concerns over dual-use export licences, that the FSR has been brought into technical dialogue, and that listing and delisting procedures are becoming more transparent.
This should help both sides maintain political support for the negotiating process. The statement also establishes clear milestones for follow-up engagement, including a ministerial video conference in January 2027 and a third regular meeting in March, providing opportunities to review implementation.
My overall assessment is that we are now seeing a limited but tangible easing of tensions, supported by concrete outcomes. Both sides still appear to be making a serious effort to avoid a full-scale trade confrontation.
On October 8–9, 2026, China’s Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao and European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maroš Šefčovič held the second meeting of the China-EU Trade and Investment Consultation Mechanism (hereinafter referred to as the “Mechanism”) in Beijing. The two sides held pragmatic and productive discussions and agreed on a list of outcomes and common understandings.
Both sides reaffirmed their commitment, as key trading partners, to properly managing their differences within the framework of World Trade Organization (WTO) rules, and to continuing to stabilise bilateral economic and trade relations while making them more balanced.
